definition_zh: 机械装置；机械结构；机制；机理；途径
definition_en: a set of connected moving parts, or an abstract arrangement of parts and processes that produces a particular result
core_image: 一排咬合的齿轮：每一枚只做一件事，连起来却推动整台机器
scene: 钟表匠掀开旧钟的后板，让里面的构件露出来。 The clockmaker lifted the back plate to show the mechanism of the old tower clock.
sceneCN: 这里 mechanism 是「机械结构、传动装置」（第 2 个义项：机器内部一起工作的部件与结构）；句意：钟表匠揭开后板，展示这座老塔钟的机械结构。场景要点：塔钟的黄铜后板、层层咬合的齿轮、钟表匠手里的放大镜；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A set of moving parts
senses.definition: the parts of a device that move together to perform a particular action
senses.definitionCN: 装置中一起运动、完成特定动作的那些部件
senses.example: The locking mechanism jammed after years of use.
senses.exampleCN: 使用多年之后，锁具装置卡住了。
senses.why: Greek mēkhanē named a device, and the first English sense was the structure of a machine. The physical set of parts is the core image in its most concrete form.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 mēkhanē 指装置，英语最早的义项就是机器的结构。这一套实体部件，就是核心意象最具体的形态。

senses.title: The working structure inside a machine
senses.definition: the arrangement and interaction of a machine's parts, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 机器各部件作为整体时的排列与相互作用
senses.example: He explained the mechanism of the clock, gear by gear.
senses.exampleCN: 他一个齿轮一个齿轮地讲解这座钟的机械结构。
senses.why: Once the parts are seen together, attention shifts from the pieces to how they transmit motion. The word now names the logic inside the device.
senses.whyCN: 当部件被放在一起看，注意力就从零件本身转到它们如何传递运动。这个词于是命名装置内部的那套逻辑。

senses.title: An institutional mechanism
senses.definition: an established arrangement of rules, offices, and procedures that produces a result or handles a problem
senses.definitionCN: 由规则、机构和程序构成的既定安排，用来产生某种结果或处理某个问题
senses.example: The treaty set up a mechanism for settling border disputes.
senses.exampleCN: 这项条约建立了一套解决边界争端的机制。
senses.why: Institutions can be read as parts of a machine: each office turns one wheel, and the arrangement yields a decision. The physical picture is applied to procedure.
senses.whyCN: 制度可以被读成机器的零件：每个机构带动一只轮子，整套安排产出一个决定。物理画面被套用到了程序上。

senses.title: A biological mechanism
senses.definition: a set of bodily or cellular processes that produces a particular effect
senses.definitionCN: 身体或细胞层面的一组过程，产生特定效果
senses.example: The immune mechanism recognises the virus within hours.
senses.exampleCN: 免疫机制在数小时内就识别出这种病毒。
senses.why: A living body also has interlocking parts, though they are cells and signals rather than gears. The image survives because the result still depends on the parts acting in order.
senses.whyCN: 活的躯体也有相互咬合的部件，只不过它们是细胞与信号，而不是齿轮。意象仍然成立，因为结果依旧依赖各部件按次序行动。

senses.title: A psychological mechanism
senses.definition: a repeated mental process by which a person copes with feelings or situations
senses.definitionCN: 一个人用来应对情绪或处境的、反复出现的心理过程
senses.example: Mocking others can work as a defence mechanism.
senses.exampleCN: 嘲笑别人可以起到防御机制的作用。
senses.why: The mind is treated as an apparatus with parts: a feeling enters, a routine process turns it, and a behaviour comes out. The word lends machinery to psychology.
senses.whyCN: 心灵被当作一台有部件的装置：一种情绪进入，一套惯常过程把它转动，一种行为出来。这个词把机械感借给了心理学。

senses.title: A reaction mechanism in chemistry
senses.definition: the step-by-step sequence by which reactants become products, including intermediate states
senses.definitionCN: 反应物变成产物的逐步序列，包括中间状态
senses.example: The reaction mechanism involves two short-lived intermediates.
senses.exampleCN: 这个反应机理涉及两种寿命很短的中间体。
senses.why: A reaction is a process with stages, and each stage hands the matter on to the next like one gear driving another. The word names the hidden chain.
senses.whyCN: 反应是一个分阶段的过程，每一阶段把物质交给下一阶段，就像一只齿轮带动另一只。这个词命名的正是那条看不见的链条。

senses.title: The philosophical doctrine of mechanism
senses.definition: the view that natural events can be explained entirely by the motion of matter, without purpose or vital force
senses.definitionCN: 认为自然事件完全可以由物质运动来解释、无需目的或生命力 的观点
senses.example: Mechanism holds that life can be explained by matter and motion alone.
senses.exampleCN: 机械论认为生命仅凭物质与运动就能得到解释。
senses.why: Here the metaphor is taken all the way: the whole of nature is declared to be one machine. The word stops naming a device and starts naming a world view.
senses.whyCN: 这里把比喻推到了底：整个自然被宣告为一台机器。这个词不再命名某个装置，而开始命名一种世界观。

senses.title: A means or channel for doing something
senses.definition: a method, channel, or route through which something can be done
senses.definitionCN: 完成某事所经由的方法、渠道或途径
senses.example: The committee has no mechanism for enforcing its decisions.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会没有执行其决定的机制。
senses.why: If a result is produced by parts working in order, then any such arrangement is a way to get the result. The concrete device thins into 'means'.
senses.whyCN: 如果结果由部件按次序工作产生，那么任何这样的安排都是取得结果的一条路。具体装置于是淡化成“手段”。

intro.en: Mechanism came into English in the 1660s from Modern Latin mechanismus, built on Greek mēkhanē 'machine, device'. The Greek-to-Latin route is clear; the deeper Indo-European link is disputed.
intro.cn: mechanism 于 17 世纪 60 年代由现代拉丁语 mechanismus 进入英语，后者建立在希腊语 mēkhanē“机械、装置”之上。希腊语到拉丁语的路径清楚；更深的印欧语关联存在争议。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'the structure of a machine, engine, or other contrivance for controlling or utilizing natural forces'. The source is Modern Latin mechanismus.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 17 世纪 60 年代，意为“机器、引擎或其他用来控制或利用自然力的装置的结构”。来源是现代拉丁语 mechanismus。

items.en: The broader sense 'a mechanical contrivance or agency of any kind' is recorded. From here the word begins to detach from literal hardware and to name any working arrangement.
items.cn: 较宽的义项“任何种类的机械装置或作用机构”有记录。自此这个词开始脱离字面上的硬件，用来命名任何一套运作安排。

items.en: Mechanismus was formed from Greek mēkhanē plus the Latin noun suffix -ismus. It is a scholarly coinage, not an inherited Latin word.
items.cn: mechanismus 由希腊语 mēkhanē 加拉丁名词后缀 -ismus 构成。它是学术性的新造词，不是继承下来的拉丁词。

items.en: Greek mēkhanē, with the Doric variant makhana, meant 'device, tool, machine', and also 'contrivance, cunning'. It is the source of machine and mechanic as well as mechanism.
items.cn: 希腊语 mēkhanē（多里斯方言作 makhana）意为“装置、工具、机械”，也有“计谋、机巧”的意思。它既是 machine、mechanic 的来源，也是 mechanism 的来源。

items.en: Watkins derived mēkhanē from PIE *magh- 'to be able, have power', the root behind may, might and magic. Beekes rejects this on formal grounds and treats the Greek word as Pre-Greek, so the deepest root is disputed and best marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 沃特金斯把 mēkhanē 追溯到原始印欧语 *magh-“能够、有力量”，该词根也是 may、might、magic 的来源。比克斯从形式证据上反对这一联系，认为这个希腊词属于前希腊语底层，因此最深词源有争议，宜标为来源不确定。

items.en: Mechanic, mechanical, mechanics, mechanize and mechanistic all belong to the same family. Mechanism keeps two lives: a concrete device, and an abstract system of parts and processes.
items.cn: mechanic、mechanical、mechanics、mechanize、mechanistic 都属于同一词族。mechanism 保有两条命：一个是具体装置，一个是由部件与过程构成的抽象系统。

note.en: The first group separates the whole machine, the mass noun, the person and the adjective. The second group compares mechanism with apparatus, device, process and system.
note.cn: 第一组区分整台机器、集合名词、人和形容词；第二组把 mechanism 与 apparatus、device、process、system 作比较。

entries.definition: a complete device with moving parts that does a job. Mechanism is the arrangement inside such a device, or the abstract version of that arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 一台有活动部件、能完成某项工作的完整装置。mechanism 是这种装置内部的排列，或这种排列的抽象版本。

entries.definition: machines as a group, or the moving parts of a machine taken as a mass. It is uncountable, while a mechanism is one countable arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 机器的总称，或作为整体看的一台机器的活动部件。它不可数，而 mechanism 是一套可数的排列。

entries.definition: a person who repairs or operates machines. It names a worker, not the working arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 修理或操作机器的人。它命名的是工人，而不是运作的结构。

entries.definition: explaining things as if they were produced by machinery. It describes a view or style, not a device.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物当作由机械产生来解释的。它描述一种观点或风格，而不是一件装置。

entries.definition: a set of equipment assembled for a particular purpose, often scientific. It names the whole set-up, while mechanism stresses how the parts work together.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定目的组装的一套设备，常用于科学场景。它命名整套装备，而 mechanism 强调部件如何一起运作。

entries.definition: an object invented to do a particular job. A device is what it is; a mechanism is how it works.
entries.definitionCN: 为完成特定工作而发明的物件。device 说的是“它是什么”，mechanism 说的是“它怎样运作”。

entries.definition: a series of actions that leads to a result. It gives the order of stages; mechanism adds the interlocking parts that carry the stages out.
entries.definitionCN: 导向结果的一系列行动。它给出阶段的顺序；mechanism 则补上执行这些阶段的咬合部件。

entries.definition: an organized set of parts or rules. It is broader than mechanism: a system may be social or biological, and it need not have a visible causal chain.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的部件或规则集合。它比 mechanism 更宽：系统可以是社会的或生物的，也不必有可见的因果链。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Greek mēkhanē 'device', machine and mechanic, and the modern family mechanical / mechanics / mechanize.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：希腊语 mēkhanē“装置”，machine 与 mechanic，以及现代词族 mechanical／mechanics／mechanize。

normal.en: Greek mēkhanē meant 'device, tool, machine'. Mechanism is the Latin-built noun for the way such a device is put together.
normal.cn: 希腊语 mēkhanē 意为“装置、工具、机械”。mechanism 是拉丁语构造的名词，指这种装置被组装起来的方式。

normal.en: Machine, mechanic and mechanism share one Greek source. The machine is the whole object, the mechanic is the person, and the mechanism is the working arrangement.
normal.cn: machine、mechanic、mechanism 共享同一个希腊来源。机器是整体物件，技师是人，机制则是运作的排列。

normal.en: Mechanical is the adjective, mechanics is the science of forces and motion, and mechanize is to replace hands with machinery.
normal.cn: mechanical 是形容词，mechanics 是研究力与运动的科学，mechanize 则是用机械取代人手。

normal.en: A defence mechanism, a reaction mechanism and a market mechanism all keep the same picture: parts in contact, each turning the next.
normal.cn: 防御机制、反应机理与市场机制都保留同一幅画面：部件相互接触，每一枚带动下一枚。

normal.en: Mechanistic is the adjective for a view that treats everything as machinery; it is a judgement about an explanation, not a description of a device.
normal.cn: mechanistic 是形容词，指把一切当作机械的看法；它是对某种解释的评判，而不是对装置的描述。

abstract.en: Picture a row of gears. No single gear can do the job alone; the result appears only when each one passes motion to the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一排齿轮。没有任何一只齿轮能独自完成工作；只有当每一只把运动传给下一只，结果才出现。

abstract.en: A mechanism is a way of hiding the work: you see a handle turn, but the useful result happens inside the box.
abstract.cn: 机制是一种把劳动藏起来的方式：你看见手柄在转，真正有用的结果却发生在盒子内部。

abstract.en: The same word serves a lock, an immune system and a treaty because all three produce a result through parts that depend on one another.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能用于一把锁、一套免疫系统和一项条约，因为这三者都通过彼此依赖的部件产出一个结果。

examples.en: The engineer traced the fault to a worn cam in the valve mechanism.
examples.cn: 工程师把故障追查到阀门装置里一只磨损的凸轮。

examples.en: Scientists still argue about the exact mechanism by which the drug works.
examples.cn: 科学家仍在争论这种药起效的确切机理。

examples.en: The two countries agreed on a mechanism for sharing river water.
examples.cn: 两国就共享河水的一套机制达成了一致。

dict_mnemonic.text: “麦克你怎”——麦克，你怎把这一排齿轮装进盒子？→ mechanism 机械装置、机制

root: 源自希腊语 mēkhanē“机械、装置”，经现代拉丁语 mechanismus 进入英语，核心是“一组咬合部件按次序把运动传下去”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of mechanism, all from one picture: interlocking parts, each doing one small job, together producing a result — whether the parts are gears, cells, institutions, or steps in a reaction.
sensesIntro.cn: mechanism 的八个义项都来自同一幅画面：相互咬合的部件，每个只做一件小事，合起来产出一个结果——无论这些部件是齿轮、细胞、机构，还是反应中的步骤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of interlocking gears, each passing motion to the next.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排咬合的齿轮，每一只把运动传给下一只。

branches.en: HARDWARE: a lock or a clock is a set of parts, and the mechanism is both the parts and the way they move together.
branches.cn: 硬件：一把锁或一座钟是一套部件，mechanism 既是这些部件，也是它们一起运动的方式。

branches.en: ARRANGEMENTS AND MEANS: institutions and procedures can be arranged like parts, and any such arrangement is a way to get a result.
branches.cn: 安排与手段：机构与程序可以像部件一样被安排，而任何这样的安排都是取得结果的一条路。

branches.en: LIFE AND MIND: immune responses and defence routines are hidden processes whose parts still depend on one another.
branches.cn: 生命与心灵：免疫反应与防御套路都是隐藏的过程，其部件同样彼此依赖。

branches.en: CHEMISTRY: a reaction mechanism is the step-by-step chain that turns reactants into products.
branches.cn: 化学：反应机理是把反应物变成产物的逐步链条。

branches.en: PHILOSOPHY: mechanism turns the metaphor into a world view, declaring all of nature to be one machine.
branches.cn: 哲学：机械论把比喻提升为世界观，宣告整个自然就是一台机器。

intro.en: Mechanism is Greek mēkhanē fitted with a Latin noun suffix. English then adds -ical, -ics, -ize and -ation, and the same Greek root also gives machine and machinery.
intro.cn: mechanism 是希腊语 mēkhanē 装上拉丁名词后缀构成的。英语随后加上 -ical、-ics、-ize、-ation，同一个希腊词根还给出 machine 与 machinery。

latinIntro.en: Modern Latin mechanismus is a scholarly compound of Greek mēkhanē and Latin -ismus. Latin also borrowed the Greek noun as machina, which is the direct source of English machine and machinery.
latinIntro.cn: 现代拉丁语 mechanismus 是希腊语 mēkhanē 与拉丁后缀 -ismus 的学术复合词。拉丁语还把希腊名词借作 machina，这正是英语 machine 与 machinery 的直接来源。

items.meaning: a working arrangement of parts; a system that produces a result
items.meaningCN: 部件的运作排列；产生结果的机制（mēkhanē 装置 + -ismus 名词后缀）
items.example: The clock's mechanism needs cleaning every year.
items.exampleCN: 这座钟的机械结构每年都要清洗。

items.example: The body uses several mechanisms to control heat.
items.exampleCN: 身体用好几套机制来控制体温。

items.meaning: explaining things as if by machinery
items.meaningCN: 机械论的；机械式解释的（-istic 构成形容词）
items.example: A mechanistic view leaves no room for purpose.
items.exampleCN: 机械论的观点不给目的留下空间。

items.meaning: to replace manual work with machinery
items.meaningCN: 使机械化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The farm mechanized harvesting in the 1950s.
items.exampleCN: 这个农场在 20 世纪 50 年代实现了收割机械化。

items.meaningCN: 机械化（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Mechanization cut the need for seasonal labour.
items.exampleCN: 机械化减少了对季节性劳动力的需求。

items.meaning: working by machinery; done without thought
items.meaningCN: 机械的；机械式的；呆板的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The lift stopped because of a mechanical fault.
items.exampleCN: 电梯因机械故障停了下来。

items.meaning: by means of machinery; without thought
items.meaningCN: 机械地；用机械方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She answered mechanically, without listening.
items.exampleCN: 她机械地回答，根本没在听。

items.meaning: the science of forces and motion; the way something works
items.meaningCN: 力学；机械学；运作方式（-ics 表示学科）
items.example: The mechanics of the trade are taught in the first term.
items.exampleCN: 这门行业的具体运作方式在第一学期教授。

items.meaningCN: 机械师；修理工（拉丁语 mechanicus，源自希腊语）
items.example: The mechanic replaced the worn bearing.
items.exampleCN: 修理工更换了磨损的轴承。

items.meaning: a device with moving parts that does work
items.meaningCN: 机器（拉丁语 machina，源自希腊语 mēkhanē）
items.example: The machine prints two thousand labels an hour.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器每小时印两千张标签。

items.meaning: machines as a group; the working parts of a machine
items.meaningCN: 机器总称；机器的运转部件（-ery 构成集合名词）
items.example: The factory replaced its old machinery.
items.exampleCN: 工厂更换了旧机器。

items.meaning: a prefix meaning mechanical or machine-related
items.meaningCN: 表示“机械的、与机械有关的”构词成分
items.example: A mechanoreceptor responds to touch or pressure.
items.exampleCN: 机械感受器对触碰或压力作出反应。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 机器的结构（现代拉丁语新造词）

latinEntries.meaning: mechanical; a person skilled in machines

senses.title: Overflowing with feeling
senses.definition: showing much more feeling or praise than seems necessary
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）表现出远超必要的感情或赞美
senses.example: Her welcome was so effusive that the whole queue stopped to watch.
senses.exampleCN: 她的欢迎太过热情，整条队伍都停下来看。
senses.why: An old man with both arms open around a girl beside a suitcase at an airport gate.
senses.whyCN: 机场出口一位老人张开双臂抱住一个女孩，旁边放着行李箱。

senses.title: Poured out freely
senses.definition: expressed in a free and unrestrained outpouring
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）以毫无拘束的倾泻方式表达出来的
senses.example: The letter ran to six effusive pages about a single afternoon.

dict_mnemonic.text: effusive ＝ ef-（向外）＋ fus（倾倒，拉丁 fundere）＋ -ive（形容词后缀，有…性质的）＝「往外倒的」。把感情往外倒 → 热情洋溢的、溢于言表的，常带一点「过头了」的意味：effusive praise 溢于言表的赞美、an effusive welcome 热情的欢迎。同一家族：effuse 动词「流出」、effusion 名词「流出；迸发；积液」、effusively 副词、effusiveness 名词。地质学里 effusive rock 指喷出岩（熔岩倒出地表冷凝），与 intrusive 侵入岩相对。近义 gushing 更口语、更贬；demonstrative 中性，指感情外露；profuse 只说数量大（profuse thanks 连声道谢），不评价是否过头。

definition_zh: 市场结构；市场中卖者的数量与规模分布，连同进入壁垒和产品差异所构成的整体格局；产业组织理论的核心术语
definition_en: the pattern formed by the number and size distribution of sellers in a market, together with the height of entry barriers and the degree of product differentiation
core_image: 一张街区俯视图：几处摊位占地悬殊，大铺占去大半街面，小摊挤在边角，街口还横着一道进场要先交钱的栏门
scene: 一条商业街刚划好摊位，几家大铺占去大半街面，小摊只能挤在边角，街口还立着一道进场要先交钱的栏门，谁进得来、谁占得宽，一眼就能看出。 Economists use the term market structure to describe this layout of sellers.
sceneCN: 同一条街上，卖者的数量、各自占地的宽窄、进场的门槛高低，合起来构成一幅可比的格局。句中的 market structure 指「卖者数量与规模分布连同进入壁垒所形成的格局」（第 1 个义项：卖者构成与规模分布的整体形态）。图中可辨识物件：摊位俯视图、占地界线、门槛、价目牌。

senses.title: How many sellers, and how big
senses.titleCN: 卖者的数量与规模分布
senses.definition: the count of firms serving a market and the range of sizes among them
senses.definitionCN: 为同一市场供货的厂商数目，以及它们规模大小的分布
senses.example: A market structure with two hundred small bakeries differs sharply from one with three large mills.
senses.exampleCN: 两百个小面包坊构成的市场结构，与三家大磨坊构成的结构截然不同。
senses.why: structure means the way parts are put together, so the phrase first asks what parts a market contains and how much room each occupies.
senses.whyCN: structure 指各部分被组合起来的方式，因此这个短语首先问的是：一个市场由哪些部分组成，每一部分占多大位置。

senses.title: Concentration of market share
senses.titleCN: 份额向少数厂商集中的程度
senses.definition: the share of the market held by the largest firms, and whether that share is spread or piled up
senses.definitionCN: 最大几家厂商所占的份额，以及该份额是分散还是堆积在一处
senses.example: The market structure is highly concentrated, with four firms holding most of the sales.
senses.exampleCN: 该市场结构高度集中，四家厂商握有大部分销量。
senses.why: once the sizes are known, the next structural question is how they add up: a few large blocks or many small ones make different shapes.
senses.whyCN: 一旦知道规模，下一个结构问题便是它们如何加总：几块大石与一堆小石形成不同的形状。

senses.title: The height of entry barriers
senses.definition: the cost, legal obstacle or technical requirement that a newcomer must meet to start selling
senses.definitionCN: 新来者要开始销售必须跨过的成本、法律障碍或技术要求
senses.example: Licensing rules and a costly pipeline give the incumbents a market structure that few challengers can enter.
senses.exampleCN: 执照规则与昂贵的管线成本，使在位者拥有一个少有挑战者能进入的市场结构。
senses.why: a structure is held up by walls as much as by contents, and the wall around a market is the barrier that keeps new sellers out.
senses.whyCN: 结构的维持既靠内容也靠围墙，而市场周围的围墙就是挡住新卖者的壁垒。

senses.title: The degree of product differentiation
senses.definition: how far rival sellers offer goods that buyers treat as distinct rather than interchangeable
senses.definitionCN: 相互竞争的卖者所提供的货物，被买方视为有区别而非可互换的程度
senses.example: Branding gives shampoo a market structure in which each label is a separate niche.
senses.exampleCN: 品牌化使洗发水形成一种市场结构，每个标签都是一个独立的细分位。
senses.why: differentiation changes the shape of a market because a market of identical goods behaves like one block, while a market of distinct goods behaves like many.
senses.whyCN: 差异化会改变市场的形状，因为同质货物市场如同一整块，而彼此有别的货物市场则像许多块。

senses.title: A type in the competition typology
senses.titleCN: 按竞争程度划分的类型标签
senses.definition: a category such as perfect competition, oligopoly or monopoly assigned to a market by its seller pattern
senses.definitionCN: 依据卖者格局给市场指定的类别，如完全竞争、寡头或垄断
senses.example: Textbooks label the airline market structure as an oligopoly because a few carriers dominate each route.
senses.exampleCN: 教科书把航空市场结构标为寡头，因为每条航线都由少数承运者主导。
senses.why: because the phrase describes a shape, it became the name of a shelf of shapes, and each shelf is a textbook type rather than a single case.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个短语描述形状，它便成了存放各种形状的架子名，每一格都是一类教科书类型，而非单一实例。

senses.title: An index used in merger review
senses.titleCN: 合并审查中可测量的指标
senses.definition: a measurable summary of seller shares, such as a concentration ratio, used by regulators to judge a proposed merger
senses.definitionCN: 对卖者份额的可测概括，如集中率，供监管机构评判拟议合并
senses.example: Regulators computed the post-merger market structure before allowing the deal.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构先算出合并后的市场结构，才允许这笔交易。
senses.why: competition law needs a number rather than a diagram, so the phrase shifted from a description of shape to a statistic that can be computed.
senses.whyCN: 竞争法需要数字而非图样，于是这个短语从「形状描述」转为「可计算的统计量」。

senses.title: A shape that changes over time
senses.definition: the shifting pattern produced by entry, exit, mergers and consolidation within a market
senses.definitionCN: 由进入、退出、合并与整合在市场内造成的变化着的格局
senses.example: Deregulation altered the market structure as new carriers entered and older ones merged.
senses.exampleCN: 放松管制改变了市场结构：新承运者进入，旧承运者合并。
senses.why: the phrase can name a process as well as a snapshot, since the arrangement of sellers is never fixed and consolidation keeps redrawing it.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语既可指名一个瞬间，也可指名一个过程，因为卖者的排列从不固定，整合不断把它重画。

senses.title: A layered pattern in platform markets
senses.titleCN: 平台市场中的分层格局
senses.definition: the arrangement of a platform market into layers, where the owner of the interface and the data sits above the sellers who depend on it
senses.definitionCN: 平台市场分成若干层的排列方式：掌握接口与数据的所有者居于依赖它的卖者之上
senses.example: A marketplace app creates a market structure in which thousands of sellers depend on one ranking system.
senses.exampleCN: 一个集市应用造出一种市场结构，成千上万的卖者依赖同一套排序系统。
senses.why: structure can also mean the layering of levels, so the phrase extends naturally to markets where one firm controls the layer through which all trade passes.
senses.whyCN: structure 也可指层次的叠加，因此这个短语自然延伸到「一家公司掌管所有交易必须穿过的那个层」的市场。

intro.en: Market structure joins a Latin trade noun to a Latin building noun. Market goes back to mercatus, a place of trading built on merx 'goods'; structure goes back to structura, a fitting together, from struere 'to pile up, to build'.
intro.cn: market structure 把一个拉丁的「交易」名词与一个拉丁的「建造」名词接在一起。market 上溯 mercatus「交易场所」，基于 merx「货物」；structure 上溯 structura「拼合、构造」，出自 struere「堆叠、建造」。

items.en: Mercatus named a market and the trading done in it, formed from mercari 'to trade', which rests on merx (genitive mercis) 'goods'. The deeper origin of merx is uncertain, and older forms proposed for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: mercatus 指市场及其中进行的买卖，出自动词 mercari「做买卖」，而该动词基于 merx（属格 mercis）「货物」。merx 的更早来源不确定，为它提出的更古形式属重构形式。

items.en: Struere meant 'to pile up, to build, to arrange in order'. It is generally thought to descend from a root meaning 'to spread out', but that earlier form is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: struere 意为「堆叠、建造、按序排列」。一般认为它源自表示「铺展开」的词根，但那个更早的形式是重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: Structura, from struere, meant the act of building and the arrangement that results, as when stones are laid in a deliberate order rather than heaped at random.
items.cn: structura 出自 struere，指建造的动作以及由此形成的排列，就像石头被有意按序砌起，而非随意堆放。

items.en: English took structure through Old French in the fourteenth century, first as the process of building and later as the internal arrangement of parts in a body, a sentence or a society.
items.cn: 英语于十四世纪经古法语借入 structure，最初指建造过程，后来指身体、句子或社会中各部分的内部排列。

items.en: The full phrase took shape in twentieth-century industrial organization, where the arrangement of sellers was linked to their conduct and to the results a market delivers.
items.cn: 完整短语在二十世纪的产业组织理论中成形，在那里，卖者的排列被与它们的行为以及市场所交付的结果联系起来。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin root of struere is unsettled, and the exact first use of the English phrase is not established, so any earlier citation offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：struere 在拉丁语之前的词根无定论，英语短语的确切首见年代亦无定说，因此为它给出的更早书证均属重构。

note.en: Group one shares the word market and is often mistaken for the target; group two names related aspects of the same industrial landscape but at a different level of analysis.
note.cn: 第一组共用 market 一词，常被误当作目标短语；第二组指同一产业图景中的相关侧面，但分析层次不同。

entries.definition: The splitting of customers into groups with shared traits; it describes demand and marketing, not the number and size of sellers.
entries.definitionCN: 把顾客按共同特征分成若干群；它描述需求与营销，而非卖者的数量与规模。

entries.definition: The way prices and signals coordinate buyers and sellers; it explains the working of a market, not its shape.
entries.definitionCN: 价格与信号协调买卖的方式；它解释市场的运作，而非市场的形状。

entries.definition: The portion of sales held by a single firm; it is one measurement used to describe the target, not the target itself.
entries.definitionCN: 单一厂商所占的销量比例；它是描述目标格局的一项测量，而非格局本身。

entries.definition: The mix of agriculture, manufacturing and services across an economy; it works one level above the arrangement of sellers in a single market.
entries.definitionCN: 一个经济体中农业、制造业与服务业的构成；它比单一市场内卖者的排列高一个层次。

entries.definition: The degree to which output is gathered in a few firms; it measures the second dimension of the target while leaving barriers and differentiation aside.
entries.definitionCN: 产出集中于少数厂商的程度；它只测量目标格局中的第二个维度，搁下壁垒与差异化。

entries.definition: The ability of a firm to raise price without losing all its customers; it is what a given arrangement allows, not the arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 厂商提价而不失去全部顾客的能力；它是某种格局所容许的结果，而非格局本身。

entries.definition: A single obstacle that keeps newcomers out; it is one ingredient of the target rather than the whole pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 阻挡新来者的单项障碍；它是目标格局中的一味成分，而非整个形态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real building root behind structure, real relatives and real textbook labels.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：structure 背后真实的「建造」词根、真实同族词以及真实的教科书标签。

normal.en: Structure comes from struere 'to pile up, to build': stones laid in a deliberate order, not heaped at random.
normal.cn: structure 出自 struere「堆叠、建造」：石头被有意按序砌起，而不是随意堆成一堆。

normal.en: The same root builds construct, instruct, obstruct and infrastructure, all of which carry an idea of putting parts together.
normal.cn: 同一词根还构成 construct、instruct、obstruct 与 infrastructure，这些词都带「把部分拼起来」的意思。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the dimensions: concentrated market structure, fragmented market structure, market structure analysis.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各个维度：集中型市场结构、分散型市场结构、市场结构分析。

normal.en: The textbook shelf holds perfect competition, oligopoly and monopoly, and each is a type of market structure.
normal.cn: 教科书那一格放着完全竞争、寡头与垄断，每一种都是一个市场结构类型。

normal.en: The old triad links structure to conduct and to performance, so the shape is studied for what it makes firms do.
normal.cn: 旧有的三段式把结构、行为与绩效连在一起，研究形状是为了看它促使厂商做什么。

abstract.en: Picture an aerial photo of a market district: two warehouses, a row of kiosks and a gate at the only road in.
abstract.cn: 想象一张市场街区的俯拍：两座仓库、一排小亭，以及唯一一条进路上的一道门。

abstract.en: Picture a handful of large stones dropped into a jar of gravel: the same total weight, but a very different shape.
abstract.cn: 想象几块大石落进一罐碎石：总重一样，形状却全然不同。

abstract.en: Picture a stadium where one owner controls the gate, the seating chart and the list of who may sell snacks inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一座体育场，同一个人掌管入口、座位表以及谁能在场内卖零食的名单。

examples.en: The market structure of the region is fragmented, with no firm holding more than a tenth of sales.
examples.cn: 该地区的市场结构是分散的，没有一家厂商的销量超过一成。

examples.en: Before approving the merger, the authority asked how the deal would change the market structure.
examples.cn: 在批准合并之前，主管机关询问这笔交易将如何改变市场结构。

examples.en: Over three decades, deregulation and consolidation reshaped the market structure of the industry.
examples.cn: 三十年间，放松管制与整合重塑了该产业的市场结构。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「market（市场）+ structure（结构）」——把集市画成一张俯视图，看几个摊位、各占多宽、门口有没有门槛，这张图就是市场结构。

root: 拉丁 mercatus「市场、交易」← mercari「做买卖」← merx（属格 mercis）「货物」；拉丁 structura「建造、构造」← struere「堆叠、建造」；英语于十四世纪经古法语借入 structure，短语为二十世纪产业组织理论术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of drawing: first count the sellers and weigh their sizes, then ask how the shares pile up, what wall keeps newcomers out and how unlike the goods are; the drawing is then given a textbook name, turned into an index, replayed as a film of change and finally extended to the layered architecture of a platform.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一次「作图」展开：先数卖者、量大小，再问份额如何堆积、什么墙挡住新来者、货物彼此有多不同；这张图随后被赋予教科书名称、被折算成指标、被当作变化的过程重放，最后延伸到平台的分层架构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bird's-eye plan of a market district, showing how many stalls there are, how much ground each holds and where the gate stands.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张市场街区的俯视图，标出有多少摊位、各自占多宽的地面、门开在哪里。

branches.en: WHO AND HOW MUCH: the number of sellers and the way their shares stack up are the first two lines of the drawing.
branches.cn: 谁与多少：卖者的数量与份额的堆叠方式，是这张图最先画的两笔。

branches.en: WALLS AND DIFFERENCES: barriers fix who can enter, while differentiation decides whether buyers see one block or many.
branches.cn: 围墙与差异：壁垒决定谁能进来，差异化决定买方看到的是一整块还是许多块。

branches.en: NAME AND NUMBER: the same drawing is filed under a textbook type and then reduced to a computable index.
branches.cn: 名称与数字：同一张图先被归入某个教科书类型，再被约简为可计算的指标。

branches.en: TIME: entry, exit and merger keep redrawing the plan, so the structure is also a process.
branches.cn: 时间：进入、退出与合并不断重画这张图，因此结构同时是一个过程。

branches.en: LAYERS: in a platform market the drawing gains a storey, and the owner of that storey sits above every seller.
branches.cn: 层次：在平台市场中，这张图多出一层，而那一层的所有者居于所有卖者之上。

intro.en: The phrase is two Latin nouns glued together in English: a trade noun ending in -atus and a building noun ending in -ura, each with its own small family.
intro.cn: 这个短语是两个拉丁名词在英语中的并置：一个带 -atus 后缀的交易名词，一个带 -ura 后缀的建造名词，各自带着自己的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin struere and structura stand behind structure and its relatives; mercatus and merx stand behind market and merchant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 struere 与 structura 在后，衍生 structure 及其亲属词；mercatus 与 merx 在后，衍生 market 与 merchant。

items.example: The root survives in commerce and merchant as well as market.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根除 market 外，还留存于 commerce 与 merchant。

items.structure: suffix forming a noun of act or result
items.meaning: the doing of something, or its outcome
items.meaningCN: 动作的进行，或动作的结果
items.example: Mercari plus the suffix gives mercatus, the trading.
items.exampleCN: mercari 加这个后缀得到 mercatus，即买卖这件事。

items.structure: Latin root in struere, 'to pile up, build'
items.meaning: to lay in order, to build
items.example: The root carries the picture of stones stacked in rows.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「石头成排砌起」的画面。

items.example: Struere supplies both the building and the arranging sense.
items.exampleCN: struere 同时提供「建造」与「排列」两层意思。

items.structure: suffix forming a noun of result
items.meaning: the thing produced by an act
items.example: Struere plus the suffix yields structura, a built arrangement.
items.exampleCN: struere 加这个后缀得到 structura，即被建成的排列。

items.example: Structura named both the act of building and its result.
items.exampleCN: structura 既指建造的动作，也指其结果。

items.example: Structure moved from building work to the plan of any whole.
items.exampleCN: structure 从建造工程转指任何整体的构成。

items.meaningCN: 属于排列本身的；结构的
items.example: Structural flaws cannot be fixed by painting over them.
items.exampleCN: 结构性的缺陷无法靠刷一层漆来修补。

items.meaning: to build by putting parts together
items.example: The same root builds, and so the verb means to put together.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根意为建造，因此这个动词意为拼合。

items.example: The restructuring closed two plants and merged the sales teams.
items.exampleCN: 重组关掉两家工厂，并合并了销售团队。

definition_zh: 濒危的；有灭绝危险的；受到威胁的
definition_en: in danger of dying out completely, especially of a species whose numbers have fallen dangerously low
core_image: 一只动物站在不断缩小的一块浮冰上，四周的水面一步步逼近
scene: 这里指「濒危的」。 The last wild population is endangered by poaching and habitat loss.
sceneCN: 这里 endangered 指「有灭绝危险的」（第 1 个义项：种群数量降到危险低位，随时可能彻底消失）；句意为最后的野生种群正受盗猎与生境丧失的威胁。图中可辨识物件：缩小的浮冰、逼近的水面、远处的枪影、被砍倒的树线。

senses.title: A species at risk of dying out
senses.definition: having so few individuals left that the species may soon disappear
senses.definitionCN: 剩余个体太少，该物种可能很快消失
senses.example: The last wild population is endangered by poaching and habitat loss.
senses.exampleCN: 最后的野生种群正受盗猎与生境丧失的威胁。
senses.why: endanger means to put into danger, and the adjective simply says the danger is now upon the species.
senses.whyCN: endanger 意为「使陷入危险」，形容词就是说明危险已经落到该物种头上。

senses.title: A legal listing status
senses.titleCN: 法律上的濒危名录身份
senses.definition: formally listed by a government as a species in danger of extinction, with protection attached
senses.definitionCN: 被政府正式列入有灭绝危险的物种名录，并附带保护措施
senses.example: The fish was declared endangered under the act in 1985.
senses.exampleCN: 这种鱼在 1985 年依据该法被列为濒危。
senses.why: a statute cannot protect a vague condition, so the adjective became a formal status that a government can list, fund and enforce.
senses.whyCN: 法律无法保护一种模糊的状况，因此这个形容词变成政府可以列名、拨款与执行的正式身份。

senses.title: The middle rung of a ranking
senses.titleCN: 受威胁等级中的一档（低于极危）
senses.definition: the category between vulnerable and critically endangered on a conservation ranking
senses.definitionCN: 保护等级排序中介于易危与极危之间的一档
senses.example: The species moved from vulnerable to endangered last year.
senses.exampleCN: 该物种去年从易危升为濒危。
senses.why: once conservationists ranked risk, the word became a rung on the ladder rather than a vague alarm.
senses.whyCN: 当保护工作者给风险排序，这个词就成了阶梯上的一档，而不再是模糊的警报。

senses.title: A habitat or ecosystem under threat
senses.titleCN: 受威胁的生境或生态系统
senses.definition: said of a habitat or ecosystem whose existence is threatened
senses.definitionCN: 指生存受到威胁的生境或生态系统
senses.example: The endangered wetland supports three rare orchids.
senses.exampleCN: 这片受威胁的湿地养着三种稀有兰花。
senses.why: a place can be at risk just as a species can, so the adjective attaches to the ground itself when the ground may disappear.
senses.whyCN: 地点也像物种一样会陷入危险，因此当地面本身可能消失时，这个形容词就落到土地上。

senses.title: A language losing its speakers
senses.titleCN: 使用人数锐减、可能消亡的语言
senses.definition: said of a language whose speakers are falling and may stop using it altogether
senses.definitionCN: 指使用者不断减少、可能彻底停用的语言
senses.example: The endangered dialect survives in two villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这门濒危方言只在两个村子里留存。
senses.why: a language is carried by speakers, so the same adjective fits when the number of carriers falls sharply.
senses.whyCN: 语言由使用者承载，因此当承载者数量骤减时，同一个形容词同样适用。

senses.title: A craft or tradition at risk
senses.titleCN: 濒临失传的手艺或传统
senses.definition: said of a practice that few people still perform and that may vanish
senses.definitionCN: 指已少有人实践、可能消失的做法
senses.example: Copper engraving is an endangered craft in this region.
senses.exampleCN: 铜版雕刻在这一带是濒临失传的手艺。
senses.why: a craft exists only while hands practise it, so it can be endangered in exactly the way a species is.
senses.whyCN: 手艺只在有人动手实践时存在，因此它可以像物种一样濒危。

senses.title: Simply in danger
senses.titleCN: 泛指处于危险之中（旧义）
senses.definition: in danger generally, of a person, reputation or plan, as in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 泛指人或名誉、计划处于危险，属较早用法
senses.example: His reputation, endangered by the rumour, needed a public answer.
senses.exampleCN: 受流言所危的名誉需要一次公开回应。
senses.why: the general sense came first, and the species sense is the specialization that took over in the twentieth century.
senses.whyCN: 一般义先出现，物种义是 20 世纪接管主导的特殊化用法。

senses.title: Threatened by a named agent
senses.titleCN: 由某个具体威胁因子所危及
senses.definition: put at risk by a stated cause, which the passive construction usually names
senses.definitionCN: 由句中明说的原因置于险境，被动结构通常点出该原因
senses.example: The colony is endangered by rising sea temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 该群落正受海温上升的威胁。
senses.why: the verb-like frame endangered by keeps the original verbal force visible inside the adjective.
senses.whyCN: endangered by 这一结构让原本的动词力量在形容词里仍然可见。

intro.en: Endangered is en- plus danger plus -ed. Danger comes through Old French from Vulgar Latin dominiarium 'power of a lord', from dominus 'lord'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: endangered 由 en- 加 danger 再加 -ed 构成。danger 经古法语来自通俗拉丁 dominiarium「领主的权力」，源自 dominus「领主」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Dominus 'lord, master' produced Vulgar Latin dominiarium 'power to command', which Old French shortened to dangier.
items.cn: dominus「领主、主人」产生通俗拉丁 dominiarium「支配之权」，古法语把它压缩为 dangier。

items.en: In Old French dangier meant 'dominion, power over someone', and only later 'risk, peril'; English took the later sense.
items.cn: 古法语 dangier 意为「支配、对某人的权力」，较晚才转为「风险、危险」；英语吸收的是较晚的义项。

items.en: English danger is recorded from the thirteenth century, and by the fourteenth it meant peril rather than power.
items.cn: 英语 danger 在 13 世纪有记录，到 14 世纪已指危险而非权力。

items.en: The verb endanger is recorded in the fifteenth century and the adjective endangered in the seventeenth, both meaning 'put or be in peril'.
items.cn: 动词 endanger 在 15 世纪有记录，形容词 endangered 在 17 世纪，二者都表示「使／处于危险中」。

items.en: The conservation sense dates from the mid twentieth century; the United States passed an Endangered Species Preservation Act in 1966 and a stronger Endangered Species Act in 1973.
items.cn: 保护义始于 20 世纪中期；美国 1966 年通过《濒危物种保存法》，1973 年通过更强的《濒危物种法》。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest citation for endangered applied to a species is not precisely recorded, and the shift of dangier from 'power' to 'peril' has competing explanations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：endangered 用于物种的最早书证没有确切记录；dangier 从「权力」转向「危险」的过程存在多种解释。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same danger family that are easily confused; group two holds the risk labels that conservation uses in a fixed order.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 danger 词族、容易混淆的形式；第二组是保护工作按固定次序使用的风险等级标签。

entries.definition: Describes something that can harm others, such as a dangerous road. Endangered describes something that may be harmed.
entries.definitionCN: 描述会伤害他者的事物，如危险的道路；endangered 描述可能受到伤害的对象。

entries.definition: To put something at risk; endangered is the resulting state, and endangered by names the agent.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物陷入危险；endangered 是结果状态，endangered by 点出施害者。

entries.definition: The state of being at risk, or the act of putting something at risk; it is used in law and in language studies.
entries.definitionCN: 指处于风险的状态或使之陷入风险的行为；用于法律与语言研究。

entries.definition: The peril itself; endangered says that this peril has attached to a particular species or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 指危险本身；endangered 说明这种危险已落到某个物种或事物上。

entries.definition: In United States law, a species likely to become endangered soon; it sits below endangered in severity.
entries.definitionCN: 在美国法律中指很可能在近期变为濒危的物种；严重程度低于 endangered。

entries.definition: Likely to be harmed because of weakness or exposure; in conservation it is a milder category than endangered.
entries.definitionCN: 因脆弱或暴露而容易受损；在保护等级中比 endangered 轻。

entries.definition: A formal synonym for put in danger; it appears in conservation writing but carries no legal listing.
entries.definitionCN: 「陷入危险」的正式同义词；见于保护写作，但不带法律名录含义。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for exposure to harm; endangered is its technical, species-specific counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指暴露于伤害的日常说法；endangered 是它在物种语境中的技术化对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: en- 'in' + danger + -ed: danger has been put into the species.
normal.cn: en-「进入」+ danger + -ed：危险已被放进这个物种身上。

normal.en: The family runs endanger, endangered, endangerment, danger, dangerous.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 endanger、endangered、endangerment、danger、dangerous。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: endangered species, critically endangered, endangered language.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：濒危物种、极危、濒危语言。

normal.en: The conservation ladder runs least concern, near threatened, vulnerable, endangered, critically endangered.
normal.cn: 保护等级阶梯依次为无危、近危、易危、濒危、极危。

normal.en: Danger itself came from a word for a lord's power, not from a word for harm.
normal.cn: danger 本身来自表示领主权力的词，而非表示伤害的词。

abstract.en: Picture an animal on ice that melts a little every day.
abstract.cn: 想象一只动物站在每天缩小一点的冰上。

abstract.en: Picture a language with two old speakers and no children listening.
abstract.cn: 想象一门语言只剩两位老人会说，没有孩子在听。

abstract.en: Picture a craft kept alive by one pair of hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一门手艺只靠一双手维持。

examples.en: The orchid is endangered because its pollinator has vanished.
examples.cn: 这种兰花因传粉者消失而濒危。

examples.en: Endangered species receive legal protection on both land and water.
examples.cn: 濒危物种在陆地与水域都受到法律保护。

examples.en: The endangered language is taught in one village school.
examples.cn: 这门濒危语言在一所村校里教授。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en（放进）+ danger（危险）+ ed」——危险已经落在它头上 → 濒危的、受威胁的

root: en-（使进入）+ danger（危险，经古法语 dangier 来自通俗拉丁 dominiarium「领主之权」，源自 dominus「领主」）+ -ed。英语 endangered。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one situation: danger is placed on something, and that situation is then read as a species, a legal listing, a rank, a habitat, a language, a craft, a reputation and a named cause.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个处境展开：危险被放到某物身上，这个处境再被读成物种、法律名录、等级、生境、语言、手艺、名誉与一个被点名的成因。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an animal on a shrinking floe while the water closes in.
core.cn: 核心意象：动物站在缩小的浮冰上，水面步步逼近。

branches.en: DANGER ATTACHED: from a species to an old reputation, the peril is real and present.
branches.cn: 危险附着：从物种到旧式名誉，危险都真实而当下。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL LABELS: law lists it, and rankings place it on a ladder.
branches.cn: 制度标签：法律把它列名，等级把它放上阶梯。

branches.en: PLACE AT RISK: a habitat can be endangered as well as its inhabitants.
branches.cn: 地点受危：生境本身也会濒危，不只有其中的生物。

branches.en: PRACTICE FADING: languages and crafts lose their carriers.
branches.cn: 实践式微：语言与手艺失去承载者。

branches.en: NAMED CAUSE: the passive frame asks who or what is doing the endangering.
branches.cn: 点明成因：被动结构追问是谁或什么在施加危险。

intro.en: Endangered is a native English construction of prefix plus noun plus suffix, built on a French borrowing rather than on a Latin root.
intro.cn: endangered 是英语本族的前缀加名词再加后缀的构造，基底是法语借词，而非拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is dominus 'lord', which gives dominiarium, then Old French dangier, then English danger; en- and -ed are English affixes.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁基底是 dominus「领主」，由此得 dominiarium，再经古法语 dangier 得英语 danger；en- 与 -ed 是英语词缀。

definition_zh: 土著的；原住民的；土生的；原始的
definition_en: belonging to the people or species that were present in a place from the earliest times
core_image: 从土地最深处长出来的第一代人，脚与泥土连在一起
scene: 博物馆的展柜里摆着世代居住在河谷的人使用过的工具。 The exhibition honours the aboriginal people of the river valley.
sceneCN: 这里 aboriginal 是「原住民的」（第 1 个义项：最早居住在某地的人群）；句意为展览致敬河谷的原住民。

原住民；土著居民

senses.title: Of a land's first peoples
senses.definition: belonging to the peoples who lived in a region before others arrived
senses.definitionCN: 属于在其他群体到来之前就居住于某地的人群
senses.example: The museum works with aboriginal communities.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆与原住民社群合作。
senses.why: Latin ab origine means 'from the beginning'; the people who were there from the beginning are named by that phrase.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ab origine 意为「从最初开始」；从一开始就在那里的人，正是由这个短语命名的。

senses.title: Native to a region
senses.definition: of a plant or animal, native to a place rather than introduced
senses.definitionCN: 指动植物原产于某地，而非外来引入
senses.example: The park protects several aboriginal species.
senses.exampleCN: 这座公园保护着几种本土物种。
senses.why: The 'from the beginning' idea applies to living things as well: a species that was there first is aboriginal to the land.
senses.whyCN: 「从最初开始」的观念也适用于生物：最早就在那里的物种，对这片土地而言就是土生的。

senses.title: Original and earliest
senses.definition: existing from the earliest period, before later changes
senses.definitionCN: 存在于最早时期、早于后来变化的
senses.example: The study traces aboriginal forms of the language.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究追溯这种语言最早的形式。
senses.why: Anything that dates from the beginning can be called aboriginal, including ideas and language forms.
senses.whyCN: 任何始于最初的事物都可称为 aboriginal，包括观念与语言形式。

senses.title: Of Aboriginal Australia
senses.definition: relating to the Indigenous peoples of Australia
senses.definitionCN: 与澳大利亚原住民族群有关的
senses.example: She studies aboriginal art from the north.
senses.exampleCN: 她研究北部的原住民艺术。
senses.why: In Australian English the capitalized Aboriginal is the standard term for the continent's first peoples.
senses.whyCN: 在澳大利亚英语中，大写的 Aboriginal 是称呼该大陆最早居民的通用术语。

senses.title: Of a native culture
senses.definition: belonging to the culture of a place's first inhabitants
senses.definitionCN: 属于某地最早居民的文化
senses.example: The festival celebrates aboriginal traditions.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节日庆祝原住民传统。
senses.why: Culture is one of the things a first people carries, so the adjective naturally attaches to its songs, stories, and rites.
senses.whyCN: 文化是原住民族所承载的事物之一，因此这个形容词自然附着于他们的歌谣、故事与仪式。

senses.title: Growing in its native range
senses.definition: growing naturally in the area where it evolved
senses.definitionCN: 在它演化所在的地区自然生长
senses.example: These aboriginal grasses survive long droughts.
senses.exampleCN: 这些原生草种能挺过漫长干旱。
senses.why: A plant that has always grown in a region is a first inhabitant of that soil, and the word borrows the human image.
senses.whyCN: 一直在某地生长的植物，是那片土壤最早的居民，这个词借用了人的意象。

senses.title: Inherited from early ancestors
senses.definition: coming from the earliest ancestors of a group
senses.definitionCN: 来自某个群体最早的祖先
senses.example: The elders keep aboriginal knowledge of the seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 长者们保存着祖先传下的季节知识。
senses.why: Knowledge that passes from the first inhabitants is treated as part of the same inheritance.
senses.whyCN: 从最早居民传下来的知识，被视为同一份遗产的一部分。

senses.title: Untouched and original
senses.definition: describing a landscape or condition before outside change
senses.definitionCN: 形容在外部改变之前的地貌或状态
senses.example: The valley remains in its aboriginal state.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷仍保持原始状态。
senses.why: Landscapes untouched by later settlement are imagined as still standing at the beginning.
senses.whyCN: 未被后来定居改变的地貌，被想象成仍停在最初的样子。

intro.en: Aboriginal is built directly from a Latin phrase meaning 'from the beginning', and it preserves that phrase almost transparently.
intro.cn: aboriginal 直接由意为「从最初开始」的拉丁短语构成，几乎透明地保留了那个短语。

items.en: ab is a Latin preposition meaning 'from, away from'.
items.cn: ab 是拉丁语介词，意为「从、离开」。

items.en: origo meant 'a beginning, source, birth'; it also produced origin and original.
items.cn: origo 意为「开端、源头、出生」，也衍生出 origin 与 original。

items.en: The phrase ab origine, 'from the beginning', was used of peoples and things present from the first.
items.cn: 短语 ab origine 意为「从最初开始」，用于从一开始就存在的人群与事物。

items.en: The plural Aborigines named the first inhabitants of a region in Roman writing.
items.cn: 复数 Aborigines 在罗马文献中指某地最早的居民。

items.en: English aboriginal appears in the seventeenth century as an adjective for the earliest inhabitants.
items.cn: 英语 aboriginal 在十七世纪出现，作形容词指最早的居民。

items.en: The term spread to botany, geology, and Australian usage, where Aboriginal names the continent's first peoples.
items.cn: 这个术语扩展到植物学、地质学与澳大利亚用法；在那里，Aboriginal 指该大陆最早的居民。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, adverb, and related origin words; the second gathers adjectives for what was there first.
note.cn: 第一组收名词、副词与相关的「起源」词；第二组收表示「最早就在那里」的形容词。

entries.definition: A member of the first people of a region; the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「原住民、土著居民」，是形容词背后的名词形式。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'from the beginning or in the original state'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「最初地、原初地」。

entries.definition: The quality of being original to a place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「原初性、本土性」，指属于某地原初事物的性质。

entries.definition: The point where something begins; from the same Latin noun origo.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「起源」，来自同一个拉丁名词 origo。

entries.definition: Born or growing naturally in a particular place.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「土生土长的、原产的」，指在某地自然出生或生长。

entries.definition: Belonging to a place by birth or natural growth.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「本地的、天生的」，指因出生或自然生长而属于某地。

entries.definition: Existing from the start, before copies or changes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最初的、原来的」，指在复制或改变之前就存在。

entries.definition: Belonging to an early stage of development.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「原始的」，指属于发展的早期阶段。

entries.definition: Coming before all others in time or order.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最早的、第一的」，在时间或顺序上先于其他。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks work from the Latin phrase ab origine and the common policy collocations; the abstract hooks picture the first feet on the land.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点来自拉丁短语 ab origine 与常见政策搭配；抽象记忆点想象最早踏上这片土地的脚。

normal.en: Aboriginal is literally ab origine, 'from the beginning'.
normal.cn: aboriginal 字面就是 ab origine，即「从最初开始」。

normal.en: Aboriginal people and aboriginal rights are standard public-policy phrases.
normal.cn: aboriginal people 与 aboriginal rights 是标准公共政策短语。

normal.en: Origin, original, and aboriginal all share the Latin noun origo.
normal.cn: origin、original 与 aboriginal 都共享拉丁名词 origo。

normal.en: In Australian English, Aboriginal with a capital letter names the continent's first peoples.
normal.cn: 在澳大利亚英语中，大写的 Aboriginal 指该大陆最早的居民。

normal.en: The adjective also works for plants and landscapes that were there first.
normal.cn: 这个形容词也适用于最早就在那里的植物与地貌。

abstract.en: Picture bare feet pressing into soil that no one else has walked on.
abstract.cn: 想象赤脚踩进无人走过的泥土。

abstract.en: Picture a seed already in the ground before any fence is built.
abstract.cn: 想象围栏尚未建起，种子早已在土里。

abstract.en: Picture a hand painting the same pattern that ancestors painted on rock.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手画出祖先曾画在岩石上的同一个图案。

examples.en: The law recognizes aboriginal land rights.
examples.cn: 法律承认原住民的土地权利。

examples.en: Several aboriginal languages are endangered.
examples.cn: 几种原住民语言濒临消亡。

examples.en: The valley still holds aboriginal forest.
examples.cn: 这个山谷仍保有原始森林。

sensesIntro.en: The senses start with the first peoples, then extend to native species, earliest forms, Australian usage, culture, plants, inherited knowledge, and untouched landscapes.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从最早的居民开始，扩展到本土物种、最早形式、澳大利亚用法、文化、植物、祖传知识与未开发的地貌。

core.cn: 核心意象：最早踏上未动过的土地的双脚

branches.en: Human first peoples, including the capitalized Australian term.
branches.cn: 人类中最早的居民，包括澳大利亚的大写用法。

branches.en: Plants and animals native to a place from the start.
branches.cn: 从一开始就原产于某地的动植物。

branches.en: Earliest forms of language and knowledge passed down.
branches.cn: 传下来的最早语言形式与知识。

branches.en: The culture carried by a place's first inhabitants.
branches.cn: 某地最早居民所承载的文化。

branches.en: Landscapes still in their original, unchanged state.
branches.cn: 仍保持原初、未被改变的地貌。

definition_zh: 减弱；减退；缓解；降低；废除
definition_en: to become less strong, intense, or numerous, or to make something less so
core_image: 正在退去的潮水：水位一点点往下落
scene: 暴雨敲了一整夜，天快亮时风声渐渐松了下来。 By morning the storm had abated and the streets were quiet.
sceneCN: 这里 abate 是「强度减弱」（第 1 个义项：风暴等自然力量变弱）；句意为到早晨风暴已经减弱，街道安静下来。

pos.zh: 减弱；减退；缓和
使减弱；降低；废止

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「减弱；减免；废止」
由否定前缀加过去分词构成，义为「未减弱的；不减的」
由动词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「减轻者；消除者」

senses.title: Of a storm: to become weaker
senses.definition: of wind, rain, or a storm, to lose force
senses.definitionCN: 指风、雨或风暴失去力量
senses.example: The storm abated before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明前风暴减弱了。
senses.why: The Old French verb abatre meant 'to beat down'; a storm that is beaten down loses its force, and the image survives in every later use.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词 abatre 意为「打下去」；被压下去的风暴失去力量，这个意象一直留到后来的所有用法里。

senses.title: Of pain or fever: to subside
senses.definition: of pain, fever, or a symptom, to become less severe
senses.definitionCN: 指疼痛、发烧或症状变得不那么严重
senses.example: The fever abated after the medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 服药之后，发烧退了。
senses.why: Illness is pictured as a force pressing on the body; when that pressure is beaten down, the symptom subsides.
senses.whyCN: 疾病被想象成压在身体上的一股力量；这股压力被压下去，症状也就减轻了。

senses.title: Of anger: to cool down
senses.definition: of anger, excitement, or tension, to become calmer
senses.definitionCN: 指怒气、激动或紧张变得平静
senses.example: His anger abated once he heard the full story.
senses.exampleCN: 听完完整经过后，他的怒气平息了。
senses.why: Emotions rise like weather; the same verb that describes a dying storm describes a temper losing its heat.
senses.whyCN: 情绪像天气一样升起；描述风暴渐息的那个动词，也同样描述脾气退热。

senses.title: Of numbers: to decrease
senses.definition: to fall in amount, rate, or number
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、比率或数目上下降
senses.example: Inflation showed no sign of abating.
senses.exampleCN: 通胀没有任何减弱的迹象。
senses.why: From wind and fever the word extends to anything measurable that rises too high and then comes down.
senses.whyCN: 从风与发烧，这个词扩展到任何升得过高、随后回落的可测量事物。

senses.title: To reduce a charge
senses.definition: to make a rent, tax, or charge smaller
senses.definitionCN: 使租金、税款或费用变少
senses.example: The landlord agreed to abate the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 房东同意减免租金。
senses.why: A charge is a burden laid on someone; abating it is beating that burden down to a lighter weight.
senses.whyCN: 费用是压在某人身上的负担；abate 就是把这副担子打下去、减轻重量。

senses.title: Legal: to remove a nuisance
senses.definition: to end or remove a nuisance, especially by legal order
senses.definitionCN: 终止或消除妨害，尤指依法律命令
senses.example: The court ordered the factory to abate the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 法院命令工厂消除噪音。
senses.why: A nuisance is a harm that keeps pressing on a neighbourhood; the law uses the old beating image to say that the harm must be pushed down.
senses.whyCN: 妨害是持续压在社区上的一种损害；法律借用古老的「打压」意象，表示必须把这股损害压下去。

senses.title: Legal: to quash a writ
senses.definition: to render a legal writ or action void
senses.definitionCN: 使某项令状或法律诉讼失效
senses.example: The writ was abated when the defendant died.
senses.exampleCN: 被告死亡后，令状被废止。
senses.why: In law the image turns administrative: an action that can no longer stand is beaten down and declared void.
senses.whyCN: 在法律里，这个意象转为程序性的：无法继续的诉讼被压下去，宣告失效。

senses.title: To lessen something
senses.definition: to make pressure, risk, or intensity less
senses.definitionCN: 使压力、风险或强度变小
senses.example: The new policy abated the pressure on hospitals.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策减轻了医院的压力。
senses.why: The transitive use simply puts the same beating action into someone's hands: an agent lowers the force instead of waiting for it to fall.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法只是把同样的「打压」动作交到某人手里：由人主动降低力量，而不是等它自己落下。

intro.en: Abate comes from a French verb meaning 'to beat down', which goes back to the Latin verb for beating.
intro.cn: abate 来自一个意为「打下去」的法语动词，后者可追溯到表示「打」的拉丁语动词。

items.en: battuere meant 'to beat, strike'; it also lies behind English battle and battery.
items.cn: battuere 意为「打、击」，英语 battle 与 battery 也源自它。

items.en: A reconstructed compound of ad- 'to' and battuere gave the sense 'to beat down'; the form is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: 由 ad-（向）与 battuere 构成的重构词，得到「打下去」之义；这一形式是重构的，并非实际文献所载。

items.en: abatre meant 'to knock down, fell, destroy', and its figurative sense 'to lessen' was already present.
items.cn: abatre 意为「击倒、砍倒、摧毁」，其比喻义「减弱」当时已经存在。

items.en: English abaten is recorded from the fourteenth century with the sense 'to diminish'.
items.cn: 英语 abaten 自十四世纪有记录，意为「减少、减弱」。

items.en: Medical and legal senses were added later, including the abatement of a nuisance or a writ.
items.cn: 医学与法律义项是后来增加的，包括消除妨害与废止令状。

note.en: The first group gathers words sharing the Latin verb for beating; the second gathers verbs for things becoming smaller or weaker.
note.cn: 第一组收共享拉丁语「打」这一动词的词；第二组收表示事物变小变弱的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for a reduction in strength, amount, or a legal charge.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「减弱、减少、减免」，指强度、数量或费用的降低。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning that something continues without any reduction.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「未减弱的」，表示某事毫无减弱地持续。

entries.definition: A partial refund; it comes from the same French verb for beating something back.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「折扣、退款」，同样来自那个表示「打回去」的法语动词。

entries.definition: A set of connected cells, or the act of beating; both go back to Latin battuere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电池组」或「殴打」，二者都可追溯到拉丁语 battuere。

entries.definition: A formal discussion; it shares the beating root through the idea of striking words together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「辩论」，经由「话语交锋」的观念共享同一个「打」的词根。

entries.definition: Of a storm, flood, or feeling, to sink to a lower level.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「平息、退去」，指风暴、洪水或情绪降到较低水平。

entries.definition: To become or make smaller in size, amount, or importance.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「减少、缩小」，指在大小、数量或重要性上变小。

entries.definition: To reduce in degree or extent.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「减轻、减少」，指在程度或范围上降低。

entries.definition: To become gradually smaller or weaker over time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「逐渐减少」，指随时间慢慢变小或变弱。

entries.definition: Of tides or energy, to flow back and decline.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「退潮、衰退」，指潮水或精力退回、减弱。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the legal collocation, the storm image, and the noun family; the abstract hooks turn the falling water level into three pictures.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用法律搭配、风暴意象与名词词族；抽象记忆点把下落的水位化成三幅画面。

normal.en: Abate a nuisance is a standard legal phrase for removing a harmful condition.
normal.cn: abate a nuisance 是标准法律短语，表示消除有害状况。

normal.en: A storm abates; the same verb appears in weather reports and in news about inflation.
normal.cn: 风暴会 abate；同一个动词也出现在天气播报和通胀新闻里。

normal.en: Unabated means the force never dropped, as in 'the storm continued unabated'.
normal.cn: unabated 表示力量从未下降，如「风暴持续不减」。

normal.en: Abatement is the noun, common in rent abatement and noise abatement.
normal.cn: 名词 abatement 常见于减租与降噪的说法中。

normal.en: The -ate ending marks a verb, and the French source verb meant to beat down.
normal.cn: -ate 结尾标明动词，法语来源动词意为「打下去」。

abstract.en: Picture a tide pulling back from a stone pier, leaving the steps dry.
abstract.cn: 想象潮水从石码头退去，把台阶留在干燥处。

abstract.en: Picture a flame turned down by a knob until it is only a blue ring.
abstract.cn: 想象火焰被旋钮调小，只剩一圈蓝光。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd's noise thinning out until the hall is almost silent.
abstract.cn: 想象人群的喧闹渐渐稀疏，直到大厅几乎无声。

examples.en: The wind abated just after sunset.
examples.cn: 日落之后风就减弱了。

examples.en: Nothing could abate her grief.
examples.cn: 什么都无法减轻她的悲伤。

examples.en: The council moved to abate noise from the highway.
examples.cn: 市议会着手降低高速公路的噪音。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额贝特」——像把音量键往下拨，额度一格格变小，声音就轻了。

root: 古法语 abatre（击倒、打下去），源自拉丁语 battuere（打）+ ad-（向）；核心义是「把力量打下去」

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from physical forces losing strength, through body and emotion, to measurable amounts and to legal actions that are cancelled.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从自然力量失去强度，经过身体与情绪，走到可计量的数量，最后是被撤销的法律行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: floodwater dropping down the marked steps of a pier
core.cn: 核心意象：洪水沿着码头刻度的台阶一层层退落

branches.en: Natural and bodily pressure falls away: storm, fever, and anger all lose heat.
branches.cn: 自然与身体的压力退去：风暴、发烧与怒气都失去热度。

branches.en: Measurable quantities fall: rates, numbers, and levels come down.
branches.cn: 可计量的数量下降：比率、数目与水平回落。

branches.en: A burden is made lighter by an agent: charges are cut and pressure is eased.
branches.cn: 人主动减轻负担：费用被减免，压力被缓解。

branches.en: A harmful condition is removed by legal order.

senses.title: The act of limiting
senses.definition: the act of keeping something within bounds, or the state of being kept within them
senses.definitionCN: 把某物保持在范围之内的动作，或受此约束的状态
senses.example: The limitation of outdoor gatherings began in October.
senses.exampleCN: 户外聚集的限制从十月开始。
senses.why: The noun comes from a Latin verb meaning to bound, so the act of drawing the line is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词出自意为「划界」的拉丁动词，画线这个动作是最古老的义项。

senses.title: A rule that restricts
senses.definition: a rule, condition or cap that restricts what may be done, used or claimed
senses.definitionCN: 限制可以做什么、用多少或主张什么的规则、条件或上限
senses.example: The contract places a limitation on how many copies may be made.
senses.exampleCN: 合同对可以制作多少份副本设了限制。
senses.why: Once a line is drawn, people need it written down, and the written line is this sense.
senses.whyCN: 线一旦画出，人们就需要把它写下来，写下来的线就是这一义项。

senses.title: A cap on money or time
senses.definition: a fixed upper amount of money, time or resources allowed for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某项用途所允许的金钱、时间或资源的固定上限
senses.example: There is a strict limitation on the daily water supply.
senses.exampleCN: 每日供水量有严格上限。
senses.why: Budgets and clocks are the most concrete boundaries, so the word settles there first.
senses.whyCN: 预算与时钟是最具体的边界，这个词先在这里落脚。

senses.title: A weakness of a method
senses.definition: a shortcoming in a study, method or tool that limits what its results can support
senses.definitionCN: 研究、方法或工具中的不足，限制了其结果能支撑的结论
senses.example: Every study states its limitations so that readers know how far the findings can travel.
senses.exampleCN: 每项研究都要说明自己的局限，读者才知道结论能走多远。
senses.why: Science uses the plural to admit what a design cannot see, and that candour is part of the method.
senses.whyCN: 科学用复数形式承认设计看不到的东西，这种坦白本身就是方法的一部分。

senses.title: The statute of limitations
senses.definition: the legal time limit within which a claim must be brought before it is barred
senses.definitionCN: 必须在期限之内提起诉讼、逾期即丧失胜诉权的法定时限
senses.example: The claim was dismissed because the limitation had expired.
senses.exampleCN: 由于时效已过，这项请求被驳回。
senses.why: Law puts a clock on every right, and the time limit is named after the limiting itself.
senses.whyCN: 法律给每项权利都装上时钟，这个时限就以「限制」这个动作为名。

senses.title: A cap on liability
senses.definition: a contractual maximum on the amount one party must pay for loss or damage
senses.definitionCN: 合同规定的、一方对损失或损害必须支付的最高金额
senses.example: The insurer accepted a limitation of liability of two million.
senses.exampleCN: 保险人接受了二百万的责任限额。
senses.why: Risk is made bearable by naming the worst number in advance, and the clause is named after that cap.
senses.whyCN: 事先把最坏的数字写出来，风险才可承受，这条款便以那个上限命名。

senses.title: A limit on an estate or right
senses.definition: a legal restriction on how long an estate or right may last or how it may pass
senses.definitionCN: 对某项地产或权利存续时间或转让方式的法定限定
senses.example: The deed carried a limitation on the sale of the land.
senses.exampleCN: 这份契据对土地的出售作了限定。
senses.why: Property law inherited the Roman boundary word and uses it for estates cut down to a fixed term.
senses.whyCN: 财产法继承了罗马的边界词，用它指被限定为固定期限的产权。

senses.title: A caveat in an argument
senses.definition: a qualification attached to a claim so that it is not taken too broadly
senses.definitionCN: 附加在主张之上的限定条件，使其不被过度推广
senses.example: He added a limitation: the rule holds only for small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 他加了一个限定：这条规则只适用于小公司。
senses.why: A wise claim fences its own reach, and the fence is called a limitation.
senses.whyCN: 审慎的主张会替自己围出边界，这道围栏就叫限定。

senses.title: A boundary in space
senses.definition: an outer boundary or edge, the oldest physical sense of the root
senses.definitionCN: 外部的边界或边缘，是这个词根最古老的具体含义
senses.example: The limitation of the old city wall still shows on the map.
senses.exampleCN: 旧城墙的边界在地图上仍看得出来。
senses.why: The Latin word meant a frontier between fields, and every later sense is a descendant of that ditch.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词本指田地之间的地界，后来所有义项都是那条沟的后代。

intro.en: Limitation comes from Latin limitare 'to bound', from limes, 'boundary, frontier'. The line of descent is clear; the exact date of the English noun is uncertain.
intro.cn: limitation 来自拉丁语 limitare「划界」，出自 limes「边界、前线」。词源线索清楚，这个英语名词出现的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Limes meant a boundary line, a frontier between fields or between provinces of the empire.
items.cn: limes 意为边界线，是田地之间或帝国行省之间的分界线。

items.en: The verb limitare meant to mark a boundary and, by extension, to keep something within it.
items.cn: 动词 limitare 意为标出边界，引申为把某物留在边界之内。

items.en: Limitio and limitatio named the marking of a bound, a word of surveyors and lawyers.
items.cn: limitio 与 limitatio 指划定边界，是测量员与法律人的用语。

items.en: The noun entered English in the fifteenth century through legal and scholarly French; the exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词在十五世纪经由法律与学术法语进入英语；确切年代不确定。

items.en: Modern English split the word two ways: the limitations of a study, and the limitation of liability in a contract.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词分成两支：研究的局限，以及合同中的责任限额。

items.en: The statute of limitations gave the word a clock, naming the period beyond which a right cannot be pursued.
items.cn: 诉讼时效法规给这个词装上了时钟，指超过之后权利便无法追索的期间。

note.en: The first group shares the boundary root or looks close; the second group holds the words that often stand in for limitation in argument and in law.
note.cn: 第一组或共享「边界」词根，或字形相近；第二组是论证与法律中常替代「限制、局限」的词。

entries.definition: The plain noun and verb for a boundary or a cap.
entries.definitionCN: 最朴素的边界或上限名词，也可作动词。

entries.definition: Restricted in amount or scope, the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 在数量或范围上受限制的形容词。

entries.definition: The drawing of a boundary, especially between states or fields.
entries.definitionCN: 划定边界，尤指国界或领域之间。

entries.definition: To remove something; it looks like the same family but comes from limen, a threshold.
entries.definitionCN: 清除某物；看似同族，其实出自意为「门槛」的 limen。

entries.definition: Occupying a threshold or in-between state, from limen rather than limes.
entries.definitionCN: 处于门槛或过渡状态，出自 limen 而非 limes。

entries.definition: A rule that prevents something, often imposed by authority.
entries.definitionCN: 阻止某事的规则，通常由权威施加。

entries.definition: A factor that forces a choice, close to limitation in research writing.
entries.definitionCN: 迫使作出选择的因素，在研究写作中接近「局限」。

entries.definition: A failure to reach a standard, the plain word for a weakness.
entries.definitionCN: 未能达到标准，是最朴素的「缺点」说法。

entries.definition: A disadvantage that makes something less attractive.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物吸引力下降的不利之处。

entries.definition: A warning or condition attached to a claim or permission.
entries.definitionCN: 附在主张或许可之上的警告或条件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real frontier word, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「边界」词、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Limes meant the frontier of the empire, so a limitation is a line drawn at the edge of what is allowed.
normal.cn: limes 指帝国的前线，限制就是画在允许范围边缘的一条线。

normal.en: The family runs limit, limited, limitless and delimitation.
normal.cn: 同族词有 limit、limited、limitless 与 delimitation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: limitations of the study, time limitation, limitation of liability.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：研究的局限、时间限制、责任限额。

normal.en: In law the plural has a life of its own: the statute of limitations.
normal.cn: 在法律里复数形式自成一体：诉讼时效。

normal.en: Eliminate and liminal are false friends; they come from limen, a threshold.
normal.cn: eliminate 与 liminal 是假朋友，它们出自意为门槛的 limen。

abstract.en: A limitation honestly stated is a gift to the reader, not a weakness of the writer.
abstract.cn: 老实说出的局限是给读者的礼物，而不是作者的无能。

abstract.en: Every boundary that keeps something in also keeps something out.
abstract.cn: 每道把东西圈进来的边界，也把另一些东西关在外面。

abstract.en: The line that protects also instructs; it tells you where the work begins.
abstract.cn: 起保护作用的线同时在指路，它告诉你工作从哪里开始。

examples.en: The report lists three limitations of its own method.
examples.cn: 报告列出自身方法的三处局限。

examples.en: A limitation on imports raised the price of steel.
examples.cn: 进口限制抬高了钢材价格。

examples.en: The suit was filed within the limitation period.
examples.cn: 诉讼是在时效期间内提起的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「利米泰申」——地上画一条白线，线外不许走：限制、局限

root: 拉丁语 limitare「划界」← limes「边界、前线」；经法律与学术法语于十五世纪进入英语。同族有 limit、limited、delimitation；eliminate 与 liminal 出自 limen「门槛」，属形近不同源。名词进入英语的确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all descend from one boundary: the act of bounding, a restricting rule, a cap on money or time, a weakness of method, the statute of limitations, a liability cap, a limit on an estate, a caveat in argument, and a boundary in space.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都出自同一条边界：划界之举、限制性规定、金额或时间的上限、方法的局限、诉讼时效、责任限额、对地产或权利的限定、论证中的保留，以及空间上的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white line painted across a road, with everything beyond it out of bounds.
core.cn: 核心意象：路面上画着一条白线，线外一切都不得越过。

branches.en: THE LINE ITSELF: a frontier drawn in space, and the act of drawing it.
branches.cn: 线本身：在空间里画出的边界，以及画线的动作。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN CAP: a rule or a fixed amount of money, time or water that may not be exceeded.
branches.cn: 写下来的上限：不可超过的规则，或金钱、时间、用水的定额。

branches.en: THE HONEST WEAKNESS: what a method cannot see, and the caveat that keeps a claim from spreading too far.
branches.cn: 诚实的弱点：方法看不到的东西，以及防止主张过度扩张的保留。

branches.en: THE LEGAL CLOCK AND DEED: a period after which a right is barred, and a term fixed on an estate.
branches.cn: 法律的时钟与契据：过期即失权的期间，以及为地产设定的期限。

branches.en: THE LIABILITY CAP: the worst number named in advance so that risk can be borne.
branches.cn: 责任限额：事先写出的最坏数字，好让风险可以承担。

intro.en: Limitation is a Latin boundary word turned into an abstract noun, with a family that runs through law and science.
intro.cn: limitation 是把一个拉丁边界词变成抽象名词，其词族贯穿法律与科学。

latinIntro.en: Limes and limitare are the sources; the noun ending came through Latin limitatio.
latinIntro.cn: limes 与 limitare 是来源，名词词尾经由拉丁语 limitatio 而来。

items.example: The short form is both noun and verb.

pos.zh: 名词：水圈；地球全部水体；行星的水层
