senses.title: A measurable gap between groups
senses.titleCN: 群体之间可测量的落差
senses.definition: a difference in amount or level between two groups that can be measured and compared
senses.definitionCN: 两个群体在数量或水平上可以被测量、比较的差别
senses.example: The disparity between urban and rural incomes has drawn public attention.
senses.exampleCN: 城乡收入的差距已经引起公众关注。
senses.why: The Latin word meant simply unequal; the noun keeps that neutral arithmetic sense of two things failing to match.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词本义就是「不相等」；这个名词保留了「两者对不上」的中性算术含义。

senses.title: Unequal distribution of money
senses.definition: the unequal spread of income, wealth or assets across a population
senses.definitionCN: 收入、财富或资产在一国人口中分配不均
senses.example: Wealth disparity inside the country grew faster than average income.
senses.exampleCN: 该国境内的财富悬殊比平均收入的增长更快。
senses.why: Once the gap is counted in money, the word takes on the policy charge of unfair distribution.
senses.whyCN: 一旦差距用金钱来衡量，这个词就带上了「分配不公」的政策色彩。

senses.title: Regional development imbalance
senses.definition: a persistent difference in prosperity, services or infrastructure between regions
senses.definitionCN: 不同地区在繁荣程度、公共服务或基础设施上的持续差别
senses.example: Regional disparity in hospital funding remains wide.
senses.exampleCN: 各地区在医院拨款上的差距依然很大。
senses.why: The noun was extended from people to places: a map can also be pulled out of shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从人群扩展到地方：一张地图同样可以被拉得变形。

senses.title: Gender gap
senses.definition: a difference between men and women in pay, promotion, health or representation
senses.definitionCN: 男女在薪酬、晋升、健康或代表性上的差别
senses.example: The study linked the gender disparity in promotions to biased review criteria.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把晋升中的性别差距归因于有偏向的评审标准。
senses.why: Social statistics gave the old word a new pair of columns, one for each sex.
senses.whyCN: 社会统计给这个旧词添了一对新栏目，男女各占一栏。

senses.title: Racial and ethnic difference
senses.definition: a difference in outcomes or treatment that falls along racial or ethnic lines
senses.definitionCN: 结果或待遇上沿种族、族裔界线出现的差别
senses.example: Racial disparity in school discipline has been documented for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 学校纪律处分中的种族差异已被记录了数十年。
senses.why: Where the two groups are named by race or ethnicity, the neutral gap becomes evidence of unequal treatment.
senses.whyCN: 当两组人按种族或族裔来命名时，中性的落差就变成了待遇不公的证据。

senses.title: Health outcome gap
senses.definition: a difference in illness, access to care or life expectancy between populations
senses.definitionCN: 不同人群在患病率、就医机会或预期寿命上的差别
senses.example: Health disparity between insured and uninsured patients widened during the epidemic.
senses.exampleCN: 传染病流行期间，有保险与无保险患者之间的健康差距扩大了。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the word to describe bodies that receive unequal care, not unequal numbers.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了这个词，用来描述得到不平等照护的身体，而不是不平等的数字。

senses.title: Unequal access to opportunity
senses.definition: an uneven chance to obtain schooling, jobs or advancement
senses.definitionCN: 获得教育、工作或上升通道的机会不均等
senses.example: Educational disparity begins before children enter school.
senses.exampleCN: 教育机会的差距在孩子入学之前就已开始。
senses.why: The gap is no longer a result but a starting line drawn in different places.
senses.whyCN: 这时的差距不再是结果，而是一条画在不同位置上的起跑线。

senses.title: Numerical inconsistency in records
senses.titleCN: 数据记录上的数值不一致
senses.definition: a failure of two sets of figures to agree with each other
senses.definitionCN: 两套数字彼此对不上
senses.example: Auditors found a disparity between the two ledgers.
senses.exampleCN: 审计人员发现两份账簿之间存在对不上的数字。
senses.why: The oldest sense of unequal survives in bookkeeping, where two columns should have matched.
senses.whyCN: 「不相等」最古老的含义在记账中留存下来：两栏数字本应相符。

senses.title: Difference in treatment
senses.definition: an unequal standard applied to people who are in comparable positions
senses.definitionCN: 对处境相当的人适用不同标准
senses.example: Employees complained of disparity in overtime pay.
senses.exampleCN: 员工抱怨加班费的发放标准悬殊。
senses.why: When the comparison moves from amounts to rules, disparity means one rule for two similar people.
senses.whyCN: 当比较从数量转向规则，这个词就指对两个相似的人用了两套标准。

intro.en: Latin gives disparity a clean line: a negative prefix, a root meaning equal, and a noun of state. English took the noun through French and later loaded it with social statistics.
intro.cn: 拉丁语为这个词提供了清楚的线索：一个否定前缀、一个表示「相等」的词根，以及一个表状态的名词词尾。英语经法语借入该名词，后来又让它承担社会统计的含义。

items.en: par meant equal, a match, a pair; it named things that stand level with one another.
items.cn: par 意为「相等、对等、一对」，指彼此齐平的事物。

items.en: dis- marked separation or negation, so dispar described a pair that does not stand level.
items.cn: dis- 表示分开或否定，因此 dispar 描述一对站不平齐的事物。

items.en: The abstract noun disparitas named the state itself: inequality, unlikeness.
items.cn: 抽象名词 disparitas 直接命名这种状态：不相等、不相同。

items.en: Middle French carried the noun forward, and English borrowed it in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 中世纪法语把这个名词继续传下去，英语在十六世纪借入。

items.en: The first English record is dated to the sixteenth century; the exact year is not certain, but the source line itself is not in dispute.
items.cn: 英语首见记录可定在十六世纪；具体年份不确定，但来源线索本身没有争议。

items.en: Twentieth-century social science attached the word to income, gender, race, health and regional columns.
items.cn: 二十世纪社会科学把这个词挂到收入、性别、种族、健康与地区这些栏目上。

note.en: The first group shares shape or root with disparity; the second group names neighbouring ideas of a gap or a mismatch.
note.cn: 第一组在形音或词根上与 disparity 相近；第二组是与「落差、对不上」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning markedly different or not comparable; it is the quality behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「迥然不同的、不可比的」，正是这个名词背后的性质。

entries.definition: Equality of level or status; it is the positive counterpart built on the same root for equal.
entries.definitionCN: 指水平或地位相等；是同一「相等」词根构成的正面反义对应词。

entries.definition: To speak of someone or something as of little value; it looks close but came through a French verb about lowering rank, not from the unequal pair.
entries.definitionCN: 指贬低某人或某物；形近，但来自法语表示「降低门第」的动词，并非出自「不相等」这一对词。

entries.definition: The plural form used when several gaps are counted together.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，用于把多处差距合在一起计数。

entries.definition: An unfair difference in status, wealth or opportunity; broader and more political than a measured gap.
entries.definitionCN: 指地位、财富或机会上的不公平差别；比一个可测量的落差更宽泛，也更带政治色彩。

entries.definition: The open distance between two levels or groups; plainer and less formal.
entries.definitionCN: 指两个水平或群体之间的空档；更朴素，也更口语。

entries.definition: A lack of proportion between parts, often suggesting something needs correcting.
entries.definitionCN: 指各部分比例失调，常暗示需要纠正。

entries.definition: A failure of two accounts or figures to agree; it stresses contradiction rather than social distance.
entries.definitionCN: 指两份说法或数字对不上；强调矛盾，而非社会性落差。

entries.definition: A failure of statements or figures to agree with one another; it is a mismatch in consistency, not a measured gap between groups.
entries.definitionCN: 指说法或数字彼此对不上；它是「是否一致」的失配，而不是群体之间可测量的落差。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real parts dis- and par, the real sister words parity and peer, and real statistical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的构词部件 dis- 与 par、真实的同根词 parity 与 peer，以及真实的统计搭配。

normal.en: dis- means apart, par means equal: pull equal things apart and you have a disparity.
normal.cn: dis- 表示分开，par 表示相等：把相等的东西拉开，就有了差距。

normal.en: Parity and peer share the same root, so disparity is the unequal twin of equality.
normal.cn: parity 与 peer 同根，因此 disparity 是「平等」那个词的不平等双胞胎。

normal.en: Picture a balance scale with one pan resting lower: that tilt is the gap.
normal.cn: 想象一架天平，一边盘子垂得更低：那份倾斜就是差距。

normal.en: Income disparity, gender disparity and health disparity are three real policy phrases.
normal.cn: 收入差距、性别差距与健康差距是三个真实的政策说法。

normal.en: Two columns of statistics sit side by side; disparity is the distance between them.
normal.cn: 两列统计数字并排而立；差距就是两列之间的距离。

abstract.en: A gap is not a wall: it is a distance that can be measured and therefore can be closed.
abstract.cn: 落差不是一堵墙，而是一段可以测量、因而也可以弥合的距离。

abstract.en: Every average hides a disparity: the mean is a line, and the gap is the space around it.
abstract.cn: 每一个平均值都藏着一处落差：均值是一条线，落差是线周围的空间。

abstract.en: Disparity is inequality turned into a number, which is why it can be argued about.
abstract.cn: 差距是被换算成数字的不平等，所以它才可以被争论。

examples.en: The survey found a sharp disparity between what men and women earn for the same work.
examples.cn: 调查发现，男女做同样的工作，报酬却有明显差距。

examples.en: Regional disparity in school funding has narrowed since the new formula was adopted.
examples.cn: 自从采用新的拨款公式，各地区的学校教育经费差距已经缩小。

examples.en: A disparity of two units between the inventories delayed the shipment.
examples.cn: 两份库存清单上有两个单位的出入，导致发货延迟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「迪斯帕若提」——把「相等」分开，剩下的就是差距

root: 来自拉丁语 disparitas「不相等」← dispar「不相等的」，由 dis-「分开、不」与 par「相等」构成，经中世纪法语 disparité 进入英语。词源链清楚，仅首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from a neutral measured gap through money, regions, gender, race, health and opportunity to records and treatment.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从一个中性的可测落差出发，经过金钱、地区、性别、种族、健康与机会，最后落到账目与待遇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one rubber ruler is pulled wider at one end, and its marks drift apart.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把橡皮尺的一端被拉宽，刻度随之越走越疏。

branches.en: THE NEUTRAL MEASURE: two groups simply fail to match on the same scale.
branches.cn: 中性的测量：两个群体在同一把尺子上就是对不上。

branches.en: THE MONEY AND THE MAP: income distribution and regional development pull apart.
branches.cn: 钱与地图：收入分配和地区发展各自被拉开。

branches.en: THE BODY AND THE GROUP: gender, race and health outcomes carry the gap into daily life.
branches.cn: 身体与群体：性别、种族与健康结果把落差带进日常生活。

branches.en: THE STARTING LINE: schooling and opportunity begin at different points.
branches.cn: 起跑线：教育与机会从不同的位置开始。

branches.en: THE LEDGER AND THE PAY SLIP: figures that disagree and rules applied unevenly.
branches.cn: 账簿与工资单：对不上的数字，以及适用不均的规则。

intro.en: Disparity is built from a negative prefix, a root meaning equal, and a noun ending of state.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个否定前缀、一个表示「相等」的词根和一个表状态的名词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies par, dispar and disparitas; parity is the positive noun from the same root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 par、dispar 与 disparitas；parity 是同根词构成的正面名词。

items.example: It turns equal into unequal.
items.exampleCN: 它把「相等」变成「不相等」。

items.example: The root names things that stand level.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名彼此齐平的事物。

items.example: The prefix and root first meet here.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与词根在这里首次结合。

items.example: The abstract noun adds a state ending.
items.exampleCN: 这个抽象名词加上表状态词尾。

items.example: It turns the adjective into the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成英语名词。

items.example: It forms disparate, the adjective of difference.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示差异的形容词 disparate。

items.example: The positive counterpart of disparity.
items.exampleCN: 是 disparity 的正面对应词。

items.example: The same root survives in the word for an equal.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根在表示「同等者」的词里留存。

items.example: The plural marks more than one measured gap.
items.exampleCN: 复数标记不止一处可测的落差。

derivatives.zh: 由词干加形容词词尾构成，义为「迥然不同的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「以不同方式」
由形容词加名词词尾构成，义为「互不相同的性质」

definition_zh: 贸易差额；贸易收支；（一国的）进出口差额记录
definition_en: the difference between the value of a country's exports and imports over a period
core_image: 两只秤盘被同一根横梁连着，一只装出口，一只装进口，梁停在哪里就是贸易差额
scene: 统计局的办公室里，两位分析员把一季度的出口总额与进口总额放进同一张表的两栏，看两栏相减后停在何处。 The quarterly balance of trade moved into surplus for the first time.
sceneCN: 这里指「出口与进口相减后的差额」，对应第 1 个义项：一定时期内出口总值与进口总值的净差；句意为该季度的贸易差额首次转为顺差。画面要点：统计表两栏、秤盘、横梁、季度标签。

pos.zh: 贸易差额；贸易收支（单数形式，常与 the 连用）

collocations.phrase: the balance of trade in goods
a deficit in the balance of trade

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多国或多期差额）

derivatives.zh: 平衡；余额；使平衡（短语的核心名词，语义为两端相等或相减后的余数）
均衡的（balance 加形容词后缀，指两侧相称）
失衡的（un- 加 balanced，指两侧不相称）
贸易；交易（短语的限定成分，源自古英语与低地德语中表示「路径、往来」的词）
交易活动（trade 加动名词后缀，指持续的买卖）

senses.title: The net difference between exports and imports
senses.definition: the difference between the total value of goods exported and the total value of goods imported in a period
senses.definitionCN: 一定时期内货物出口总值与进口总值的差
senses.example: The quarterly balance of trade moved into surplus for the first time.
senses.exampleCN: 该季度的贸易差额首次转为顺差。
senses.why: Latin bilanx is 'two scales', and a balance is the beam between them; applied to trade, the beam settles according to which side is heavier.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 bilanx 意为「两只有秤盘的天平」，balance 就是那根横梁；用在贸易上，横梁按哪一侧更重而停住。

senses.title: The statistical record of that difference
senses.titleCN: 记录这一差额的统计账目
senses.definition: the official account or statement that records exports and imports and their net result
senses.definitionCN: 记录进出口及其净结果的官方账目或报表
senses.example: The balance of trade is published every month.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易差额每月公布。
senses.why: A balance can be a document as well as a quantity, so the phrase names the published account itself.
senses.whyCN: balance 既可指数量，也可指文件，因此这个短语也指公布的那份账目。

senses.title: The balance in goods alone
senses.definition: the balance measured on merchandise only, as distinct from goods and services together
senses.definitionCN: 只按商品计算、与货物和服务合计相区别的差额
senses.example: The balance of trade in goods differs from the services account.
senses.exampleCN: 货物贸易差额与服务账目并不相同。
senses.why: Statistical systems keep separate ledgers, so the phrase is often qualified by the item being counted.
senses.whyCN: 统计体系分设账目，因此这个短语常被限定为所计的项目。

senses.title: A favourable or unfavourable balance
senses.definition: the older usage in which a surplus is called favourable and a deficit unfavourable
senses.definitionCN: 旧时把顺差称为有利、把逆差称为不利的用法
senses.example: Mercantilists prized a favourable balance of trade above all.
senses.exampleCN: 重商主义者把出超看得高于一切。
senses.why: Before statistics was neutral, the balance was judged by policy advantage, so one sign was praised and the other blamed.
senses.whyCN: 在统计尚未中性化之前，差额要按政策利害评判，因此一个符号受褒，另一个受贬。

senses.title: The balance as a policy indicator
senses.titleCN: 作为政策指标的贸易差额
senses.definition: the balance read as a signal of competitiveness, demand or external vulnerability
senses.definitionCN: 被读作竞争力、需求或对外脆弱性信号的差额
senses.example: A widening deficit in the balance of trade alarmed the treasury.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易差额逆差扩大使财政部警觉。
senses.why: A single number is easy to cite, so the balance became a shorthand for the health of external trade.
senses.whyCN: 一个数字便于引用，于是贸易差额成了对外贸健康与否的简称。

senses.title: The period figure as published
senses.definition: the balance reported for a month, quarter or year
senses.definitionCN: 按月、按季或按年报告的那一差额
senses.example: The monthly balance of trade beat expectations.
senses.exampleCN: 月度贸易差额好于预期。
senses.why: Because the balance is recalculated each period, the phrase often carries month, quarter or year as a qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 因为差额按期重算，这个短语常带月份、季度或年份作限定。

senses.title: Adjusting or correcting the balance
senses.definition: the balance considered as something to be improved by tariffs, currency or spending policy
senses.definitionCN: 被视为可通过关税、汇率或支出政策加以改善的差额
senses.example: The government tried to correct the balance of trade with tariffs.
senses.exampleCN: 政府试图用关税纠正贸易差额。
senses.why: Once the balance is a number to be managed, verbs such as correct, improve and rebalance attach to it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦差额成为可管理的数字，纠正、改善、再平衡这类动词就会与它搭配。

senses.title: Any equilibrium between inflow and outflow
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：流入与流出之间的均衡
senses.definition: an abstract state of equilibrium between what enters and what leaves a system
senses.definitionCN: 某系统流入与流出之间达成均衡的抽象状态
senses.example: The balance of trade between the two regions shaped their politics.
senses.exampleCN: 两地区之间的进出往来格局塑造了它们的政治。
senses.why: The image of two pans can be applied to anything that flows in and out, not only to goods across a border.
senses.whyCN: 两只秤盘的意象可用于任何有进有出的事物，而不只是跨境货物。

intro.en: Balance of trade joins balance, from Latin bilanx 'two scales', with trade, a word of path and exchange. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: balance of trade 把出自拉丁 bilanx「两只有秤盘的天平」的 balance，与表示「路径与往来」的 trade 组合起来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lanx meant a scale pan or a dish, and it named the shallow vessel on which goods were weighed.
items.cn: lanx 意为秤盘或浅盘，指称货时所用的浅器皿。

items.en: Bi- 'two' plus lanx gave bilanx, an adjective for a pair of scales, and the noun balance kept that image.
items.cn: bi-「二」加 lanx 构成 bilanx，指一对秤盘的形容词，名词 balance 保留了这一意象。

items.en: Old French balance meant both the instrument and the equality it shows, and English took it in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 balance 既指器具，也指它显示的相等，英语在 13 世纪吸收了这个词。

items.en: In the seventeenth century a favourable balance of trade meant exports exceeding imports, and the phrase became a goal of policy.
items.cn: 在 17 世纪，有利的贸易差额指出口超过进口，这个说法成为政策目标。

items.en: Modern statistical offices made the balance of trade a routine monthly figure, neutral in sign but political in use.
items.cn: 现代统计机构把贸易差额变成按月发布的常规数字，符号中性，用途却带政治性。

note.en: The first group shares the scale image or looks close to it; the second group names related accounts and measures.
note.cn: 第一组共享天平意象或与之外形相近；第二组是相关的账目与指标。

entries.definition: The beam and pans, or a state of equality; alone it can mean a bank balance or physical steadiness.
entries.definitionCN: 横梁与秤盘，或相等的状态；单独使用时也可指银行余额或身体平衡。

entries.definition: The record of all transactions with the world, including services, income and transfers; the trade balance is one part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 与世界的全部交易记录，含服务、收入与转移；贸易差额只是其中一部分。

entries.definition: A near synonym of balance of trade, used more often in headlines and tables.
entries.definitionCN: 贸易差额的近义说法，更常用于标题与表格。

entries.definition: The Latin adjective for a two-pan scale; it is the etymological root, never used in modern English trade talk.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中「双盘天平」的形容词；它是词源根，现代英语贸易语境中不用。

entries.definition: A negative balance, when imports exceed exports.
entries.definitionCN: 差额为负的情形，即进口超过出口。

entries.definition: A positive balance, when exports exceed imports.
entries.definitionCN: 差额为正的情形，即出口超过进口。

entries.definition: Exports minus imports in national accounts; it is the same quantity expressed inside a formula.
entries.definitionCN: 国民核算中出口减进口；它是同一数量在公式中的表达。

entries.definition: The balance of physical goods only, excluding services, which are called invisible trade.
entries.definitionCN: 只计实体货物的差额，不含被称为无形贸易的服务。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real two-pan root, the real trade word and real statistical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「双盘」词根、真实的贸易词与真实统计搭配。

normal.en: Balance is two pans on one beam, so the phrase is simply which pan is heavier.
normal.cn: balance 是一根横梁上的两只秤盘，所以这个短语就是看哪只盘更重。

normal.en: The Latin adjective bilanx 'two-scaled' is the root, and bi- means two.
normal.cn: 拉丁形容词 bilanx「双盘的」是词根，其中 bi- 意为二。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the uses: favourable balance, balance of trade figures, correct the balance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示用法：有利差额、贸易差额数据、纠正差额。

normal.en: The phrase is singular and usually takes the, unlike the countable trade deficit.
normal.cn: 这个短语用单数并常带定冠词，与可数的 trade deficit 不同。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with balance of payments, which also counts services and income.
normal.cn: 不要与 balance of payments 混淆，后者还把服务与收入计入。

abstract.en: Picture two pans loaded with crates, one marked out and one marked in, and the beam settling.
abstract.cn: 想象两只秤盘装满货箱，一只标着出，一只标着进，横梁缓缓停住。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where the two columns are drawn as columns of blocks, and the taller one wins.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账簿，两栏被画成积木柱，较高的那栏取胜。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway with two counters, one clicking for arrivals and one for departures.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门有两个计数器，一个为进来的人跳，一个为出去的人跳。

examples.en: The balance of trade improved as oil imports fell.
examples.cn: 随着石油进口下降，贸易差额有所改善。

examples.en: Economists watch the balance of trade for signs of demand.
examples.cn: 经济学家观察贸易差额，以寻找需求迹象。

examples.en: A favourable balance of trade was the mercantilist ideal.
examples.cn: 出超是重商主义的理想。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「两只秤盘量进出」——balance 是天平，trade 是贸易，秤停在哪边就是贸易差额

root: balance 出自拉丁 bilanx「两只有秤盘的天平」= bi-（二）+ lanx「秤盘」，经古法语进入英语；trade 源自古英语与中古低地德语中表示「路径、往来」的词。合指进出口相减后的差额。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on one beam: the net difference, the published account, the goods-only figure, the old favourable-unfavourable judgment, the policy signal, the period number, the object of correction and finally any inflow-outflow equilibrium.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都立在同一根横梁上：净差额、公布的账目、仅计货物的数字、旧式的有利不利评判、政策信号、按期发布的数字、被纠正的对象，最后是任何进出均衡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pans on one beam, one loaded with exports and one with imports.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根横梁上两只秤盘，一只装出口，一只装进口。

branches.en: BASE DIFFERENCE: the beam settles according to the heavier pan.
branches.cn: 基础差额：横梁按更重的那只盘停住。

branches.en: RECORD AND PERIOD: the difference is published and recalculated each period.
branches.cn: 记录与周期：差额被公布，并按期重算。

branches.en: SCOPE: the account can be narrowed to goods alone.
branches.cn: 范围：这本账可以收窄到只计货物。

branches.en: JUDGMENT AND ACTION: the balance is praised, watched or corrected.
branches.cn: 评判与行动：差额或被褒扬、被观察、被纠正。

branches.en: METAPHOR: any inflow and outflow can be weighed on the same beam.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何流入流出都能放在同一根横梁上称量。

intro.en: Balance of trade is a phrase whose core word is built from a Latin numeral and a Latin noun for a pan.
intro.cn: balance of trade 的核心词由一个拉丁数词与一个表示秤盘的名词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin bi- 'two' and lanx 'pan' give balance and bilanx; trade has a Germanic origin and gives trading, trader and trademark.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 bi-「二」与 lanx「秤盘」衍生 balance 与 bilanx；trade 源自日耳曼语，衍生 trading、trader 与 trademark。

senses.title: A mention
senses.titleCN: 提及：在话语或文字中说到某事物
senses.definition: an act of mentioning someone or something in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在口头或书面中说到某人或某事物的行为
senses.example: The article makes frequent reference to earlier studies.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章频繁提及早期的研究。
senses.why: Reference comes from referre 'to carry back', and a mention carries the reader's mind back to the thing named.
senses.whyCN: reference 出自 referre「带回」，而一次提及正是把读者的心思带回被命名的事物。

senses.title: A cited source
senses.titleCN: 参考文献：被引用的出处
senses.definition: a source cited in a text, or the entry that identifies it
senses.definitionCN: 正文所引用的出处，或标识该出处的条目
senses.example: Every claim in the paper has a reference at the end of the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 论文中每一处主张在句末都有参考文献。
senses.why: The same carrying-back motion now points at a document: the text sends the reader to the place where the claim came from.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「带回」动作现在指向文件：正文把读者送回主张的来源之处。

senses.title: A reference work
senses.titleCN: 工具书：供查阅而非通读的书
senses.definition: a book or database consulted for specific facts rather than read through
senses.definitionCN: 为查具体事实而查阅、而非从头读到尾的书或数据库
senses.example: The librarian keeps the dictionaries and atlases in the reference section.
senses.exampleCN: 图书管理员把词典与地图集放在参考区。
senses.why: Here the noun has become a label for a class of books whose purpose is to be referred to.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词已成为一类书籍的标签，这类书的存在就是为了被查阅。

senses.title: A recommendation
senses.titleCN: 推荐信：为求职者作证的文件
senses.definition: a letter or statement in which someone speaks in support of an applicant
senses.definitionCN: 某人为申请人提供支持的书面陈述或信件
senses.example: She asked her former manager for a reference.
senses.exampleCN: 她请前任经理写一封推荐信。
senses.why: The recommender 'refers' the employer back to facts about the candidate, so the letter is called a reference.
senses.whyCN: 推荐人把雇主「引回」候选人的事实，因此这封信叫 reference。

senses.title: A basis for comparison
senses.titleCN: 参照物：用来比较的基准
senses.definition: a standard, point or system against which other things are measured or understood
senses.definitionCN: 用于衡量或理解其他事物的标准、点或系统
senses.example: The fixed stars provided a reference for early navigators.
senses.exampleCN: 恒星为早期航海者提供了参照。
senses.why: To refer is to send something back to a fixed point; a reference point is exactly that anchor.
senses.whyCN: refer 就是把某物送回一个固定点；reference point 正是这样的锚点。

senses.title: A computing reference
senses.titleCN: 计算机引用：指向对象或地址的间接名称
senses.definition: in computing, a value that points to an object or memory location rather than holding the data itself
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中指向对象或内存位置、而非直接保存数据的值
senses.example: The function returns a reference to the cached record.
senses.exampleCN: 该函数返回对缓存记录的引用。
senses.why: Programming borrowed the everyday idea of pointing back: a reference lets the program reach the original object without copying it.
senses.whyCN: 编程借用了「指回」的日常观念：引用让程序无需复制就能抵达原对象。

senses.title: A linguistic referent
senses.titleCN: 语言指称：词语所指的对象
senses.definition: in linguistics, the object or entity in the world that a word or phrase points to
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中词语或短语所指向的现实对象或实体
senses.example: The reference of 'the mayor' depends on who holds office.
senses.exampleCN: 「市长」一词的指称取决于谁在任。
senses.why: Linguists separated the word from the thing: the expression refers, and its reference is the thing it reaches.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家把词与物分开：表达式进行指称，而它的 reference 就是所抵达之物。

senses.title: An employment inquiry
senses.titleCN: 背景查询：向原单位核实情况
senses.definition: an inquiry made to a previous employer or institution about a person's record
senses.definitionCN: 向原雇主或机构核实某人履历的查询
senses.example: The hiring manager made a reference call before the offer.
senses.exampleCN: 发出录用通知前，招聘经理打了背景核实电话。
senses.why: The HR sense extends the document sense into a process: someone is asked to refer the new employer back to the record.
senses.whyCN: 人事义把文件义扩展为过程：有人被请求把新雇主引回履历记录。

intro.en: Reference comes from Latin referre 'to carry back', built on ferre 'to bear, carry'. English took the noun through French and Medieval Latin forms, and the modern senses range from mention to citation.
intro.cn: reference 出自拉丁 referre「带回」，基于 ferre「携带、承受」。英语经由法语与中世纪拉丁形式取得该名词，现代义从「提及」一直延伸到「引用」。

items.en: Latin ferre meant 'to bear, carry, bring'. Its compounds include transfer, offer, infer, refer and prefer, each with a different prefix direction.
items.cn: 拉丁 ferre 意为「携带、运送、带来」，其复合词包括 transfer、offer、infer、refer、prefer，各前缀设定不同方向。

items.en: Referre joined re- 'back' to ferre, meaning 'to carry back, bring back, direct to'. It could refer a question to a person or a matter to a source.
items.cn: referre 把 re-「回」加到 ferre，意为「带回、拿回、指向」，可用于把问题交给某人，或把事项指向某来源。

items.en: Medieval Latin referentia and French reference supplied the noun 'a referring, a relation'. The exact route into English is uncertain in detail.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 referentia 与法语 reference 提供了「指涉、关联」的名词。进入英语的确切路径细节存疑。

items.en: English reference developed from 'relation or respect' to 'a mention', then to 'a cited source' and 'a recommendation'.
items.cn: 英语 reference 从「关联、方面」发展为「提及」，再发展为「被引出处」与「推荐」。

items.en: Computing added the pointer sense in the twentieth century, while linguistics fixed reference as the relation between expression and object.
items.cn: 20 世纪计算机领域增加了「指针」义，语言学则把 reference 固定为表达式与对象之间的关系。

items.en: The precise first English date is uncertain, and the deeper origin of ferre is discussed only as a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与传入路径）：英语最早书证确切年代存疑；ferre 的更深来源只作为重构来讨论。

note.en: The first group separates the refer family; the second gives near-synonyms for mentioning, citing or a standard of comparison.
note.cn: 第一组区分 refer 词族；第二组给出关于提及、引用或比较基准的近义词。

entries.definition: To mention, consult or direct someone to something. The noun reference names the mention or the source.
entries.definitionCN: 指提及、查阅或把某人引向某物；名词 reference 命名该提及或出处。

entries.definition: A sports official or a person who writes a recommendation. A referee is a person; a reference may be a document.
entries.definitionCN: 指体育裁判或写推荐的人。referee 是人，reference 可以是文件。

entries.definition: The act of sending someone to another doctor or service. It is the transfer, not the cited source.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某人转给另一位医生或服务；是转介行为，不是被引出处。

entries.definition: In linguistics, the actual object a word points to. Reference is the relation; the referent is the target.
entries.definitionCN: 语言学中词语指向的实际对象。reference 是关系，referent 是目标。

entries.definition: A formal quotation of a source with identifying details. It is narrower than reference, which can also mean a mere mention.
entries.definitionCN: 指带识别信息的正式引用；比 reference 窄，后者也可仅指提及。

entries.definition: An indirect or passing mention meant to be recognized. It does not provide a source.
entries.definitionCN: 指有意让人识别出的间接或顺带提及，不提供出处。

entries.definition: A rule or measure used for comparison. A reference point anchors measurement; a standard defines what counts as acceptable.
entries.definitionCN: 指用于比较的规则或尺度。参照点用于锚定测量；标准则界定何为合格。

entries.definition: The origin of information or material. A reference identifies a source, but the source is the thing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指信息或材料的来源。reference 标识出处，而 source 是那个来源本身。

entries.definition: A written statement praising a person's qualities, often for employment. It overlaps sense 4 but stresses praise.
entries.definitionCN: 指称赞某人品质的书面陈述，常用于求职；与第 4 个义项重叠，但更强调赞扬。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'back' + ferre 'carry' + -ence: carrying the mind back to a source.
normal.cn: re-「回」+ ferre「携带」+ -ence：把心思带回某个来源。

normal.en: The family runs refer, referee, referral, referendum, referential.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 refer、referee、referral、referendum、referential。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the senses: with reference to, reference book, frame of reference, letter of reference.
normal.cn: 固定搭配展示义项：关于、工具书、参照系、推荐信。

normal.en: A reference points back; a referent is the thing pointed at.
normal.cn: reference 指回，referent 是被指的东西。

normal.en: citation is formal quoting; allusion is indirect mention without a source.
normal.cn: citation 是正式引用；allusion 是不给出处的间接提及。

abstract.en: Picture a bookmark that sends your finger back to one exact page.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚书签把你的手指送回确切的一页。

abstract.en: Picture a surveyor's pole standing fixed while everything else is measured against it.
abstract.cn: 想象测量员的标杆固定不动，其余一切都以它为基准。

abstract.en: Picture a thread tied from a note to the drawer where its evidence is kept.
abstract.cn: 想象一根线把便条连到存放证据的抽屉。

examples.en: The report makes no reference to the earlier failed trial.
examples.cn: 这份报告只字未提早先那次失败的试验。

examples.en: Keep a reference list in the same style throughout the thesis.
examples.cn: 整篇论文的参考文献表要保持同一体例。

examples.en: The compass needle needs a fixed reference to show direction.
examples.cn: 罗盘指针需要一个固定参照才能显示方向。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）+ fer（带）」——把话头带回原处 → reference 提及、参考

root: 拉丁 ferre「携带」→ referre「带回、指向」→ 中世纪拉丁 referentia；英语 reference。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all point back: a mention points to a topic, a citation to a source, a reference book to facts, a letter to a record, a point to a scale, a variable to an object, a word to a referent, a call to an employer.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在「指回」：提及指向话题，引用指向出处，工具书指向事实，推荐信指向履历，参照点指向尺度，变量指向对象，词语指向指称物，核实电话指向雇主。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bookmark sending the finger back to one exact page.
core.cn: 核心意象：书签把手指送回确切的一页。

branches.en: TEXTUAL POINTING: a mention in prose, and the cited source that backs it.
branches.cn: 文本指涉：文中的提及，以及支撑它的被引出处。

branches.en: DOCUMENTS: a book made for consultation, or a letter that points an employer to a record.
branches.cn: 文件：为查阅而作的书，或把雇主引向履历的信。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: a fixed point or frame against which things are judged.
branches.cn: 测量：用于判断事物的固定点或框架。

branches.en: SYMBOLIC POINTING: a program value or a word reaches an object without being that object.
branches.cn: 符号指涉：程序值或词语抵达对象，却不等于对象本身。

branches.en: PROCEDURE: the document sense becomes a call that checks a record.
branches.cn: 程序：文件义变成核实履历的一通电话。

intro.en: Reference is a Latin verb of carrying plus a noun ending: re- 'back' + ferre 'carry' + -ence. The same root appears across a large family of English verbs of transfer.
intro.cn: reference 是拉丁「携带」动词加名词词尾：re-「回」+ ferre「携带」+ -ence。同一词根出现在大量英语「转移」动词中。

latinIntro.en: The ferre family includes refer, transfer, offer, infer, prefer, confer, differ and suffer; the shared image is bearing something from one place or person to another.
latinIntro.cn: ferre 词族包括 refer、transfer、offer、infer、prefer、confer、differ、suffer；共同意象是把某物从一处或一人带到另一处或另一人。

items.meaning: a pointing back; a mention or source
items.example: The book contains useful references to primary sources.
items.exampleCN: 这本书含有指向原始资料的有用参考。

items.example: The footnote refers to page 42.
items.exampleCN: 脚注指向第 42 页。

items.meaning: one to whom a matter is referred; an official
items.example: The referee stopped the match.
items.exampleCN: 裁判中止了比赛。

items.meaning: the act of sending someone onward
items.meaningCN: 把某人转介出去的行为
items.example: The doctor wrote a referral to a specialist.
items.exampleCN: 医生写了转诊单给专科医生。

items.structure: Latin referendum (that which must be referred)
items.meaning: a vote referred to the people
items.example: The constitution was changed by referendum.
items.exampleCN: 宪法通过全民公投得以修改。

items.example: The files were transferred to a new server.
items.exampleCN: 文件被转移到新服务器。

items.meaning: to carry a conclusion into view
items.example: We inferred the cause from the pattern.
items.exampleCN: 我们从模式推断出原因。

items.meaning: to carry before others; to favour
items.example: She prefers tea to coffee.
items.exampleCN: 她更喜欢茶而不是咖啡。

definition_en: an animal that feeds chiefly on the flesh of other animals, or a plant that traps and digests small animals

senses.title: Flesh-eating animal
senses.titleCN: 食肉动物：以动物肉为主食
senses.definition: an animal whose diet consists mainly of the flesh of other animals
senses.definitionCN: 指以其他动物的肉为主要食物的动物
senses.example: Wolves are carnivores that hunt in packs.
senses.exampleCN: 狼是成群狩猎的食肉动物。
senses.why: The word names a dietary class by its food, so a carnivore is defined by what it eats rather than by how it kills.
senses.whyCN: 这个词按食物命名食性类别，因此食肉动物由吃什么界定，而不是由如何杀界定。

senses.title: Obligate carnivore
senses.titleCN: 专性食肉：无法靠植物维生
senses.definition: a carnivore that cannot survive on plant food alone because it lacks the enzymes or gut microbes to use it
senses.definitionCN: 指因缺乏利用植物的酶或肠道微生物、无法仅靠植物维生的食肉动物
senses.example: The domestic cat is an obligate carnivore that needs taurine from meat.
senses.exampleCN: 家猫是专性食肉动物，必须从肉类获得牛磺酸。
senses.why: Physiology, not preference, makes the class: an obligate carnivore would starve on a vegetarian diet.
senses.whyCN: 决定这一类的是生理而非偏好：专性食肉者吃素会饿死。

senses.title: Apex carnivore
senses.titleCN: 顶级食肉者：成年后几无天敌
senses.definition: a carnivore at the top of its food chain that suffers little or no predation itself
senses.definitionCN: 指处于食物链顶端、自身几乎或完全不被捕食的食肉动物
senses.example: The removal of the apex carnivore let the deer herd grow unchecked.
senses.exampleCN: 顶级食肉者的消失让鹿群无限制增长。
senses.why: The label marks position rather than appetite: the top carnivore regulates the levels below it.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签标出位置而非食欲：顶级食肉者调节其下各层。

senses.title: Carnassial shear
senses.titleCN: 裂齿剪切：食肉动物的牙齿构造
senses.definition: a carnivore identified by specialised shearing teeth that slice flesh rather than grind it
senses.definitionCN: 指以专门剪切齿、切割而非研磨肉类的食肉动物
senses.example: The fossil's carnassial teeth show it was a carnivore.
senses.exampleCN: 化石上的裂齿表明它是食肉动物。
senses.why: Anatomy is evidence: paleontologists read the diet of extinct animals from the shape of their teeth.
senses.whyCN: 解剖即证据：古生物学家从牙齿形状读出已灭绝动物的食性。

senses.title: Carnivore guild
senses.titleCN: 食肉集团：共享猎物的竞争者
senses.definition: in community ecology, the set of carnivores in one habitat that partition prey by size, time or hunting method
senses.definitionCN: 群落生态学中指同一生境中按猎物大小、时间或狩猎方式分工的一群食肉动物
senses.example: The carnivore guild splits the night into separate hunting shifts.
senses.exampleCN: 食肉集团把夜晚分成不同的狩猎班次。
senses.why: Competition forces the class to divide resources, so the word becomes a unit of community structure.
senses.whyCN: 竞争迫使这一类分配资源，因此这个词成为群落结构的单位。

senses.title: Carnivorous plant
senses.titleCN: 食虫植物：捕虫并消化吸收
senses.definition: a plant that captures and digests small animals, usually insects, to obtain nutrients
senses.definitionCN: 指捕获并消化小动物（通常为昆虫）以获取养分的植物
senses.example: The pitcher plant is a carnivore that digests insects in its fluid.
senses.exampleCN: 猪笼草是一种在液体中消化昆虫的食肉植物。
senses.why: The word is borrowed for plants because the mechanism is the same: capture, kill and absorb.
senses.whyCN: 这个词被借用于植物，因为机制相同：捕获、杀死并吸收。

senses.title: Human carnivore
senses.titleCN: 人类的食肉者：以肉为主食的人
senses.definition: a person whose diet is based mainly on animal flesh, or a cultural label for meat-centred eating
senses.definitionCN: 指以动物肉为主食的人，或指以肉为中心的饮食文化标签
senses.example: The festival celebrates the region's identity as a land of carnivores.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节庆庆祝该地区作为食肉者之乡的身份。
senses.why: The zoological label becomes a cultural identity, usually light-hearted rather than clinical.
senses.whyCN: 这个动物学标签变成文化身份，通常轻松而非临床。

senses.title: The order Carnivora
senses.titleCN: 食肉目：分类学上的一个目
senses.definition: in taxonomy, the mammalian order Carnivora, which includes cats, dogs, bears and seals, some of which eat little meat
senses.definitionCN: 分类学中哺乳动物的食肉目，包括猫、犬、熊与海豹，其中有些很少吃肉
senses.example: Not every member of Carnivora is a strict carnivore; bears eat berries.
senses.exampleCN: 食肉目并非每个成员都是严格食肉者；熊也吃浆果。
senses.why: Taxonomy and diet diverge here, which is why the order name can mislead a reader about a species' food.
senses.whyCN: 分类与食性在此分岔，因此目名可能误导读者对该物种食物的判断。

intro.en: Carnivore joins Latin caro 'flesh' with vorare 'to devour', literally 'flesh devourer', and it was fixed in scientific Latin before entering English.
intro.cn: carnivore 由拉丁语 caro「肉」与 vorare「吞食」构成，字面即「吞食肉者」，先在科学拉丁语中定型，后进入英语。

items.en: Caro, carnis meant flesh, especially animal flesh, and it also gives English carnal and carnage.
items.cn: caro, carnis 意为肉，尤指动物肉，它也是英语 carnal 与 carnage 的来源。

items.en: Vorare meant to swallow or devour, the same second element as in herbivore and omnivore.
items.cn: vorare 意为吞咽、吞食，与 herbivore、omnivore 中的后半部分相同。

items.en: Carnivorus was used in modern scientific Latin for flesh-eating animals, and Cuvier's classification is usually credited with popularising it in the early nineteenth century. The exact coining is uncertain.
items.cn: carnivorus 在近代科学拉丁语中用于食肉动物；一般认为居维叶在 19 世纪早期的分类体系推广了它，但确切的造词者存疑。

items.en: English carnivore appears in the nineteenth century, and the exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 carnivore 在 19 世纪出现，确切首见书证存疑。

items.en: Carnivora was fixed as an order name, later creating the awkward fact that some carnivorans are largely herbivorous.
items.cn: Carnivora 被定为目名，后来造成一个尴尬事实：有些食肉目成员其实以植物为主食。

items.en: The nineteenth-century discovery of insect-eating plants extended carnivore to plants, where it remains a common though informal label.
items.cn: 19 世纪对食虫植物的发现把 carnivore 扩展到植物，这一标签至今常用，但属非正式说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -vore ending; the near-meaning group separates a diet class from hunting behaviour and taxonomy.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -vore 结尾；近义组区分食性类别、狩猎行为与分类学。

entries.definition: An animal that eats plants. It is the opposite diet class, differing only in the first element of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 指以植物为食的动物。它是相反的食性类别，复合词只在第一部分不同。

entries.definition: An animal that eats both plants and flesh. A carnivore may occasionally eat plants without becoming an omnivore in the classificatory sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指既吃植物也吃肉的动物。食肉动物偶尔吃植物，并不因此在分类上变成杂食动物。

entries.definition: The adjective form. Carnivore is the noun for the animal, so a plant is described as carnivorous, not as a carnivore in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词形式。carnivore 是动物的名词，因此在正式写作中植物应说成 carnivorous，而不是 carnivore。

entries.definition: One that hunts and kills. A predator may eat plants as well, and a carnivore may be a scavenger that never hunts.
entries.definitionCN: 指猎杀者。捕食者也可能吃植物，而食肉动物可能是从不狩猎的食腐者。

entries.definition: A bird of prey, or in palaeontology a grasping dinosaur. It names a hunting form, not a diet class.
entries.definitionCN: 指猛禽，古生物学中也指具抓握能力的恐龙。它命名狩猎形态，而非食性类别。

entries.definition: An animal that eats mainly insects. It is a narrower diet class that can sit inside carnivory.
entries.definitionCN: 指以昆虫为主食的动物，是更窄的食性类别，可归入食肉范畴。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: caro 'flesh' + vorare 'devour': the flesh devourer.
normal.cn: caro「肉」+ vorare「吞食」：吞食肉者。

normal.en: The family runs carnivorous, carnivory, carnassial and the order name Carnivora.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 carnivorous、carnivory、carnassial 以及目名 Carnivora。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: obligate carnivore, top carnivore, large carnivore, carnivore guild.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：专性食肉动物、顶级食肉动物、大型食肉动物、食肉集团。

normal.en: Carnivora is an order, not a diet rule: bears belong to it and still eat berries.
normal.cn: Carnivora 是一个目，不是食性规则：熊属于该目，却仍吃浆果。

normal.en: Carnal and carnage share the caro- root, which is about flesh rather than eating.
normal.cn: carnal 与 carnage 共享 caro- 词根，该词根指肉，而非吃。

abstract.en: Picture a wolf worrying a carcass while the pack waits in a ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一只狼撕扯尸体，狼群在外圈等待。

abstract.en: Picture a pitcher plant holding a fly in its fluid.
abstract.cn: 想象猪笼草把一只苍蝇泡在液体里。

abstract.cn: 想象一块化石颌骨，其中一枚刀状齿高出其余。

examples.en: Large carnivores need wide ranges and abundant prey.
examples.cn: 大型食肉动物需要广阔的活动范围与充足的猎物。

examples.en: The cat is an obligate carnivore and cannot thrive on plants.
examples.cn: 猫是专性食肉动物，无法靠植物良好生存。

examples.en: Carnivorous plants supplement their mineral intake with insects.
examples.cn: 食虫植物用昆虫补充矿物质摄入。

root: 拉丁 caro, carnis「肉」+ vorare「吞食」→ 科学拉丁语 carnivorus／carnivore「吞食肉者」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all name a flesh eater, but the boundary shifts: physiology, position in the chain, tooth shape, community role, plants and taxonomy each redraw it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指食肉者，但边界不断移动：生理、链条位置、齿形、群落角色、植物与分类学各自重新划定它。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wolf tearing at a carcass while the pack circles.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只狼撕扯尸体，狼群在外围。

branches.en: DIET AND PHYSIOLOGY: eating flesh is the base, and inability to use plants makes it obligatory.
branches.cn: 食性与生理：吃肉是基本义，无法利用植物则使它成为专性。

branches.en: POSITION AND COMMUNITY: apex carnivores and guilds describe how the class is arranged.
branches.cn: 位置与群落：顶级食肉者与食肉集团描述这一类的排列方式。

branches.en: EVIDENCE: shearing teeth let palaeontologists read diet from bone.
branches.cn: 证据：裂齿让古生物学家从骨骼读出食性。

branches.en: BOUNDARY CASES: plants and the order Carnivora both stretch the label past its diet meaning.
branches.cn: 边界个案：食虫植物与食肉目都把标签拉伸到食性义之外。

branches.en: CULTURE: human meat eating borrows the zoological word as identity.
branches.cn: 文化：人类食肉借用这个动物学词汇作为身份。

intro.en: Carnivore is the flesh branch of the -vore family, and its stem caro- also feeds words about the body and about slaughter.
intro.cn: carnivore 是 -vore 词族中的「肉」支，其词干 caro- 还衍生出关于身体与屠杀的词。

latinIntro.en: Caro, carnis is a third-declension noun for flesh, vorare a first-conjugation verb for devouring, and -vorus the adjectival form.
latinIntro.cn: caro, carnis 是第三变格的「肉」名词，vorare 是第一变格的「吞食」动词，-vorus 是形容词形式。

items.example: The forest holds three large carnivores.
items.exampleCN: 这片森林里有三种大型食肉动物。

items.example: Carnivorous fish patrol the reef edge.
items.exampleCN: 食肉鱼类巡游在礁缘。

items.example: Carnivory appears in several lizard lineages.
items.exampleCN: 食肉习性出现在好几个蜥蜴谱系中。

items.meaning: a shearing tooth of a carnivore
items.meaningCN: 食肉动物用于剪切的牙齿
items.example: The carnassial pair works like scissors.
items.exampleCN: 那对裂齿像剪刀一样工作。

items.meaning: the mammalian order of flesh eaters
items.example: Carnivora includes both hunters and berry eaters.
items.exampleCN: 食肉目既包含猎手，也包含吃浆果者。

items.example: The poem contrasts carnal appetite with reason.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗把肉体欲望与理性对照。

items.example: The battlefield was a scene of carnage.
items.exampleCN: 战场是一片屠杀景象。

items.example: Herbivores and carnivores split the grass crop.
items.exampleCN: 植食动物与食肉动物分食草料。

items.example: The omnivore takes fruit and insects alike.
items.exampleCN: 杂食动物既吃果实也吃昆虫。

definition_en: to have a particular feature as the mark that identifies, defines or typifies the thing described
core_image: 一块木牌上刻着一道深痕，检验员不看整块木料，只凭这道痕就认出它属于哪一批
scene: 地质队员站在一处河谷前，向导指着两岸的红色岩壁，说认出这套地层靠的是颗粒粗细与胶结物的颜色。 The red beds can be characterized by coarse grains and iron cement.
sceneCN: 向导在河谷边讲解地层（第 1 个义项：以某事物为主要特征）；句意为这套红色地层以粗颗粒与铁质胶结物为特征。图中可辨识物件：红色岩壁、地质锤、放大镜、记录本。
